544603|2026-03.headline: Groww's Q4 FY26 call gave no hard financial figures; equity F&O market share rose to 10.6% from 9.1%, with active derivative customers at about 17 lakh per quarter.
544603|2026-03.overview: Management's prepared remarks were high-level: FY26 was the first year as a listed company, with new launches in commodities, bonds (secondary), wealth (Fisdom, W, Prime) and an AMC partnership with SSG pending approval. Management said industry activity is still well below the peak, with FIIs negative and March 2026 volatility hitting MTF and commodity accounts. Several data requests (affluent AUM and revenue share, average MTF book, MTF share of cash ADTO, Fisdom and AMC revenue, commodity ADTO share) were deferred to follow-up. Management reiterated that cost to grow is roughly INR 450-500 crore a year and will be kept below revenue growth.

financial_highlights.change: from 9.1% in the prior quarter (about 150 bps); management said the calculation method was also changed
from about 14 lakh in the prior quarter
broadly flat year on year; expected to rise slightly and be lower than revenue growth
employee cost up QoQ, driven by investment in AMC, wealth and AI
not confirmed; to be disclosed later

segments.name: Broking (Groww platform)
segments.commentary: Equity and F&O share gains continued; F&O penetration of the customer base is about 10%, versus about 18% before November 2024. ARPU is back to pre-November 2024 levels, driven by MTF and commodities offsetting lower F&O mix.

segments.name: Wealth (Fisdom, W, Prime)
segments.commentary: Fisdom was acquired about six months ago; Prime launched in January 2026. Management said it is too early to comment on scaling or cross-sell. The shareholder letter targets Fisdom profitability by FY28.

segments.name: AMC (SSG partnership)
segments.commentary: Pending regulatory approvals. Management said AMC hiring will add cost, and AMC revenue was not disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Commodities and bonds
segments.commentary: Commodities launched a little over a year ago; commodity ADTO market share will be disclosed after the one-year mark. Bonds secondary market launched after primary.

guidance_outlook: Cost to operate (Groww platform) rises in Q1 FY27 due to a one-time appraisal increase, then stays broadly flat in absolute terms for the rest of the year, excluding risk-related costs.
Cost to serve expected to fall as a share of revenue, though absolute tech and AI costs rise.
Cost to grow expected to rise slightly from INR 450-500 crore but grow more slowly than revenue. Q1 marketing spend is seasonally higher (IPL), and FY27 spend is expected to be slightly above FY26.
Margin expansion depends on revenue growth: management said margins expand above about 15% revenue growth and more so at about 30%; they do not expand at lower growth.
Management expects FY27 to be the inflection point for AI in customer experience and productivity. No algo or API strategy yet, pending regulatory clarity.
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose QoQ, mainly due to the Fisdom acquisition.
Employee cost rose QoQ on investment in AMC, wealth and AI, with headcount at about 1,800.
No capex figures or capacity disclosures were given on the call.
demand_pricing: Industry growth: management cited about 10-15% CAGR over the long run, with step-ups in bull markets. It said the industry is still away from the bottom, with FIIs negative and tariffs weighing on sentiment.
Acquisition funnel has shifted toward mutual funds and ETFs since September 2024. SIPs remain a major source of AUM accumulation.
Customer AUM dipped on an M2M basis in March 2026, but inflows held up as most customers stayed in profit after 31 March. Management said April was better than March.
Stock advisory and MF advisory demand is among the highest voice-of-customer requests; launch timing not set.
Settlement: customers choose bill-to-bill, monthly or quarterly settlement; quarterly is the default most customers prefer.

qa_highlights.question: How have customer cohorts from 2023-24 performed through the market correction, and how does their behaviour differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition has shifted toward MF and ETF; SIP flows continue. Most customers are still profitable, and the March dip was mainly M2M. No cohort-level AUM data was given.

qa_highlights.question: Equity F&O market share jumped to 10.6% from 9.1%. What drove it, and what is the algo share?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were new customers, initiatives including 915, and higher quarterly transacting customers (about 17 lakh vs 14 lakh). Algo and API volumes are not meaningful, and there is no algo strategy yet.

qa_highlights.question: Did employee cost and depreciation rise because of Fisdom, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose mainly due to Fisdom. Employee cost rose on investment in AMC, wealth and AI. Headcount is about 1,800.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF customer profile and what is the average MTF book?
qa_highlights.answer: No study was done. MTF is mostly used by existing customers, not as an acquisition product. The average book will be disclosed later, and the peak was around end-January or February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook and the cost to acquire customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion depends on revenue growth, with about 15% as a threshold. Cost to grow is largely acquisition spend, is roughly fixed on an annual basis, and Q1 is seasonally higher.

qa_highlights.question: Industry active clients have plateaued near 50 million. What supports growth, and are there open interest limits or settlement changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth depends on bull markets; long-run industry CAGR is about 10-15%. Open interest is under half the limit on average and was not hit in Q4. Quarterly settlement is customer choice, not a regulatory mandate.

risks_watch: Market volatility: March 2026 negative balances and M2M losses in MTF and commodities were booked as risk-related cost to operate.
Regulatory risk on F&O and speculation curbs; management said it engages regulators at industry level.
Fisdom and wealth investment needs and FY28 profitability target; wealth scale-up is still early.
Pending SSG AMC approvals and AMC integration costs.
Undisclosed data: affluent AUM and revenue share, Fisdom and AMC revenue, average MTF book, commodity ADTO share, and the market-share methodology change.

544603|2026-06.headline: Groww Q1 FY27 call: management gave few hard numbers; MTF yield fixed at 14.95%, cash yields up ~5% YoY, and F&O softness attributed to volatility, not SEBI rules.
544603|2026-06.overview: Management, led by co-founders Lalit Keshre (CEO) and Ishan Bansal (CFO), framed the quarter around building a wealth management platform and launching multiple products. Credit (LAS) now makes up 34% of disbursements, bonds launched last quarter are scaling, and SEBI and CCI approvals were received for the State Street Global partnership in the AMC. Management attributed F&O and order softness to volatility and to gold/silver ETF slowdown rather than regulation, and said Q4 FY26 was an anomaly for MTF and derivatives. Several data requests were declined or deferred, including CAC detail, revenue split, Fisdom/AMC revenue, and new-customer ARPU.

financial_highlights.change: ~+5% YoY; mgmt expects +1-2 pp per quarter as MTF penetration rises

financial_highlights.metric: Customer acquisition cost (CAC) per new NTU
financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR1,400 in Q4 FY26 per analyst; ~INR1,000 in Q4 per another reference (analyst-stated)

~0.13 million (analyst-stated, flat across the two periods)

segments.commentary: MTF growth ahead of plan partly on markets; ticket size rising, but early Q2 MTF book flattish per analyst, which management tied to end-of-quarter market moves. LAS is 34% of disbursements.

segments.name: Broking (cash and F&O)
segments.commentary: Management says F&O dip in June-July tracked volatility (Iran war news), not SEBI rules. Cash order decline is mainly ETF (gold/silver) slowdown, per management. Derivatives are stabilising vs Q3.

segments.name: Commodities
segments.commentary: More than 28% retail share of notional ADTO; described as at an advanced adoption stage.

segments.name: AMC / Fisdom / Wealth
segments.commentary: SEBI and CCI approvals received for the State Street Global partnership in the AMC. Fisdom revenue has not yet shown significant improvement; W and Prime traction too early to quantify.

guidance_outlook: Cash yields expected to keep rising near term, by roughly 1-2 pp per quarter, as MTF penetration grows; no ceiling given.

Employee cost rise this quarter attributed to April appraisal cycle, not headcount; long-run headcount not expected to rise significantly.
US stocks via GIFT City license: testing underway, launch 'soon' but no firm date; to start with US stocks only.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost rise a sign of hiring for a wealth transition, and what is the 2-3 year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said the rise is mainly the April appraisal cycle, not headcount. Headcount is not expected to rise significantly, with wealth to be AI- and tech-led alongside RMs. ESOPs are about 10% of employee cost in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is MTF yield accretive for the cash business, and how far can acceptance go?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash yields are up ~5% YoY and are expected to rise 1-2 pp per quarter as MTF penetration grows. Adoption is still early, and ticket size can expand as infra issues are resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did active derivatives customers soften sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said Q4 FY26 was an exception with war-driven volatility that started in Q4. Compared with Q3, the trend is improving and stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and scope of US stock options via GIFT City, and effect of F&O margin changes?
qa_highlights.answer: US stocks licensed and in testing, launch 'soon' with no exact date; start with US stocks. On the expiry margin news, management said it cannot comment on news, and the Nov 2024 change cannot be isolated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the July F&O dip due to SEBI rules, and is the cash order decline 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the F&O dip to volatility (Iran war news), with regulation impact smaller than the industry expected and not material for Groww. The cash order decline reflects slowing ETF (gold/silver) activity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CAC rise sharply, and what is the affluent customer retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishan Bansal said the rise reflects about two months of IPL spend versus one week in Q4, with brand benefit and weaker acquisition. Affluent retention is near 100% because AUM stickiness is high.

544603|2026-09.headline: Groww's Q2 FY27 call centred on Cost to Serve rising on AI compute, one-time INR10-13 crore hit, and MTF book adding ~INR600-700 crore a quarter.
544603|2026-09.overview: Management explained that Cost to Serve rose in Q2 due to AI-related costs, higher compute on more trading days, and a one-time INR10-13 crore hit from delayed files on an expiry day. Cost to Grow fell because the IPL branding spend in Q1 did not recur. Management said the margin trading facility (MTF) book adds about INR600-700 crore a quarter on average, with volatility from stock-level moves and policy changes such as higher haircuts on crowded stocks. Other operating income rose on about 30 IPOs (including SBI AMC and NSE) and BSDA income. Management said the call was qualitative on several items, such as US stocks timing and UPI MDR outcome, and gave few new numbers on AUM or market share.

segments.name: Broking (cash and derivatives)
segments.commentary: Management said revenue in derivatives and commodities is driven by order count at INR20 per order, while cash revenue depends on both order size and count (lower of 10 bps or INR20). Cash market share has been about 15% and derivatives about 11% over the last three to four quarters, per analyst. August was the lowest volume month of Q2.

segments.name: Wealth (Groww Prime, MF Prime, Fisdom)
segments.commentary: Wealth AUM was disclosed for the first time; management said MF Prime is small. Users rose by almost 50% quarter-on-quarter, mainly from Groww Prime per analyst. Wealth income is reported within other operating income, and Fisdom users are now included in active customers.

segments.name: Lending (MTF, personal loans, loan against shares)
segments.commentary: MTF book adds about INR600-700 crore a quarter. Loan against shares was launched in the last two quarters with good early traction; personal loan book is growing gradually quarter-on-quarter. No figures were given for the lending book size.

segments.name: Other operating income
segments.commentary: Rose sequentially on about 30 IPOs in the quarter (including SBI AMC and NSE) and BSDA income. IPO and BSDA income were regrouped out of stocks revenue.

guidance_outlook: Cost to Grow for FY27 is expected to stay in the INR400-500 crore a year range, with more spend in good markets and less in weak ones.
Management expects the MTF book to keep growing, adding about INR600-700 crore a quarter, and MTF share of cash turnover to rise over time.
Management expects the CAS rule change to normalise volumes, with faster recovery depending on the effective date, which was awaited.
Management expects UPI MDR outcome to be not materially cost-changing, but the cap level (INR300 mentioned) is still under discussion with the regulator.
Management expects long-term convergence of cash and F&O market share toward NSE active share, but said this could take around 10 years.
capex_capacity: Management said 915 power-trading tools and web-based trading are not yet a material contributor to volume or revenue.
AI spend is rising: in-house AI stack being built to lower per-token cost; AI-related costs and compute costs rose in Q2.
Compute cost scales with trading days; management uses more compute on trading days and much less on non-trading days.
Company said the wealth integration (Fisdom) is complete and some products are being mainstreamed across apps.
demand_pricing: Management said competitive pricing approach is to give customers more value than they are charged, and it is not following competitors on price.
Analyst noted some discount brokers cut brokerage by half; management did not directly address this.
Volumes were affected by the CAS circular; management expects CAS changes to normalise volumes, with derivatives largely unaffected by the proposed options.
Customers using more than two products exceed 50%; over 5% use more than four products.
US stocks product is in early beta testing with good customer feedback; no timeline for full launch was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Cost to Grow fall sharply while Cost to Serve rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost to Grow fell because the Q1 IPL branding cost did not recur. Cost to Serve rose on AI-related costs, higher compute on more trading days, and a one-time INR10-13 crore hit from delayed expiry-day files.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off MTF cost in September, as in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off cost as such, though MTF costs were present. Policy changes now include higher haircuts (up to 80% on some crowded stocks) and more frequent approved-list reviews, including industry-level book checks.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order per ADTV rising while broking revenue is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Derivatives and commodity revenue is per order, not per ADTV, and cash revenue depends on the asset mix (ETFs vs small caps). Ticket size shifts drive the difference, and cash brokerage per order is about INR15-16 versus INR20 in F&O.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the NSE active market share not reflected in cash and F&O market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects convergence over the long term as customers age and trade more and MTF grows, but noted it will not be quarter-to-quarter and may take about 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UPI MDR impact on cost to serve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still awaiting the final outcome. It expects no material cost change, but the cap (INR300 discussed) is critical and the company will push to lower it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost to grow run-rate for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said around INR125 crore is the current average; H2 spend will depend on market conditions, with more spend if markets do well and less in weak markets.

risks_watch: SEBI's CAS circular outcome and effective date, which affects volume normalisation.
MTF book volatility from crowded stocks and possible haircut changes, plus policy execution risk.

Competitive pressure from brokerage cuts and AI-led tools; US stocks product still in beta.

544606|2026-03.headline: Pine Labs FY26 revenue grew about 19% with adjusted EBITDA up to Rs.559 Crores in Q4; FY27 revenue guided to 21%-23.5%.
544606|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as delivering about 19% full-year revenue growth, roughly 500 bps EBITDA margin expansion, and full-year PAT of about Rs.113 Crores. Q4 operating cash flow was about Rs.676 Crores, but management said this should not be viewed in isolation, with full-year operating cash flow at about Rs.395 Crores. Q4 growth shortfall was attributed mainly to infrastructure deployment delays (about 2 lakh POS machines backlogged due to a chip shortage) and softness in Middle East and airline business. The company gave a hard FY27 revenue growth guidance of 21%-23.5%, and said Q1 FY27 would be at the lower end.

segments.commentary: International growing about 44% per management; Philippines has five clients including GCash; POS services launched in Singapore; two head-to-head wins against global payment majors.

544606|2026-06.headline: Pine Labs Q1 FY27 revenue grew about 20% YoY, but adjusted EBITDA of Rs.126 Crores fell short of the ~Rs.135-140 Crores management said it would have liked, due to front-loaded investments.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at about Rs.126 Crores, below the level management said it wanted, after front-loaded spend on cloud, network and sales headcount (about 500 salespeople added over six months). PAT was close to Rs.20 Crores on PBT of about Rs.38 Crores, with an effective tax rate of about 46% due to losses in international entities that are not tax-recognised. Operating cash flow/working capital was about 16% of revenue against guidance to stay under 15% for the full year. DITP India growth was 20-25%, while the reported 4% DITP GTV growth was driven by bill payments with one client moving transactions in-house.

544606|2026-09.headline: Pine Labs Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 24% YoY and adjusted EBITDA about 27%; management now expects FY27 revenue growth above 23-23.5%.
544606|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as strong execution, with revenue up about 24% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up about 27%. Management said each business line (offline, issuing, online) grew faster than the market and gained share. Flow-based income rose about 25% YoY while UPI volumes grew about 50%. Management plans to add about 10 lakh soundboxes and sales headcount, and said H2 EBITDA should be well above H1 and FY EBITDA margin should be at least 21%. Analysts pressed on EBITDA margin dilution, UPI MDR economics, capex and indirect cost step-ups; management answered most with qualitative explanations and few new numbers.

segments.commentary: Management said it retained 100% of enterprise accounts with strong net revenue retention and added Tanishq across all stores in Q2.

segments.name: Mid-market offline
segments.commentary: Nearly 100,000 terminals deployed on a trailing 12-month basis; mid-market cohorts (apparel, F&B, duty free, airports) cited as growing about 39-40%.

segments.name: Issuing (prepaid and gift cards)
segments.commentary: Processing share about 80-85%; distribution grew faster than market. NCMC distribution about 1,000 cards per day, Bharat Yatra 25,000-30,000 cards per month; employee tax benefit card due end November/early December.

segments.name: Online and bill payments
segments.commentary: Top four Q-commerce companies use the gateway; one of the largest consumer billers signed up, going live in Q3.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE about 1 lakh transactions per day (Emirates NBD, Wio Bank); close to 1 lakh POS in Malaysia; 50,000 POS in Philippines; present in about 22 countries. Singapore gift card distribution reduced in Q2 after a large retailer exited, with EBITDA impact called immaterial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected above the 23-23.5% guided at start of year, per CEO closing remarks.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin expected at least 21% (CEO said 'at least 21'), versus 18% in H1 as described by analyst.
H2 EBITDA expected to be much higher than H1; EBITDA expected to keep expanding over time as flow-based income grows.
Working capital guided at 13-15% of top line for full year; Q3 seasonally weaker cash flow expected.
Contribution margin guided at 72-75% overall, with issuing 52-55% and DITP 81-83%.
Effective tax rate declined vs prior quarter; management gave medium to long-term tax guidance (no figures stated).
capex_capacity: About 10 lakh (1 million) additional soundboxes planned to capture UPI transactions at existing merchants; management said soundboxes cost about Rs.500-600 and capex impact is immaterial.
H1 capex about Rs.240 Crore, including about Rs.35 Crore slipped from Q4 FY26 and about Rs.20-25 Crore of advances (vendors now asking about 80% advance versus 20% earlier) due to chip shortages.
Full-service POS deployments continue at natural pace; not part of the 10 lakh soundbox plan.
Capex described as normalising; management expects steady state across the two years after adjusting for these items.
demand_pricing: UPI accounts for about 75-77% of POS transactions; those transactions grew about 68% compounded over last two years; management expects about 70% growth next year.

UPI MDR: 40 bps cited as the headline rate, with about 11 bps retained by acquirer; implementation timing with NPCI, which management said it does not control. Analyst's sensitivity of Rs.80-230 Crore range (from 5-6 bps to full 40 bps on about Rs.4 lakh Crore run-rate) was described as directionally correct, but management said it books income only when received.
Management said no pricing pressure in offline or online; online price increases by peers allowed Pine Labs to gain share.
Management said soundbox pricing will be transaction-based rather than a Rs.125-130 rental, as merchants will not pay both.
Affordability (EMI) growth now broader than CDIT, with non-CDIT volumes rising; October Navratri and Dussehra described as strong, Diwali read pending over about two weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Will India issuing and acquiring growth (about 40%) accelerate in Q3 given festive season timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Navratri and Dussehra were strong and Diwali visibility comes in about two weeks; growth drivers cited were new use cases such as refund wallets and gaming, not seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Does the UPI GTV outlook for FY28 (about 60% growth) rest on the device count plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tied it to UPI shift on POS (75-77% of transactions) and to 10 lakh additional soundboxes to capture missed UPI volumes at existing merchants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable GMV and take rate under the UPI MDR change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to estimate net take rate, citing commercial negotiations and possible MCC-based pricing; said only volumes were provided.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international revenue mix dip and does it affect profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to a large global retailer's exit from Singapore gift card distribution, a low-margin business; EBITDA impact called immaterial and revenue for Q2 already reflected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin tracking below last year and will guidance be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales hiring pays back over about nine months, and it does not plan to cut EBITDA guidance; expects at least 21% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex and indirect costs rise in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex overflow from Q4 (about Rs.35 Crore) and Rs.20-25 Crore advances; indirect cost includes cloud and data at 8.5-9% of top line, outsourced field staff, and GFF sponsorship which fell in Q2 this year versus Q3 last year.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash flow and working capital trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 cash flow strong but not to be extrapolated; FY net working capital expected in 13-15% of top line, with Q3 seasonally weaker.

544608|2026-03.headline: Emmvee FY26 revenue rose 116% to INR 5,049 crore and PAT 193% to INR 1,082 crore, with 9.4 GW order book and 6 GW expansion underway.
544608|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year as a listed company (IPO Nov 2025, INR 2,900 crore raised), with revenue of INR 5,049 crore, EBITDA of INR 1,734 crore (34% margin) and PAT of INR 1,082 crore (21% margin). Module capacity reached 10.3 GW after two 2.5 GW lines were commissioned (May and Dec 2025), and cell utilisation rose to 69.9% for the year and 79% in Q4. Working capital absorbed cash as inventory built up, while the 6 GW integrated cell and module project at Devanahalli is progressing with IREDA's INR 3,306 crore loan sanctioned. Management stated that FY27 will be a year of execution.

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 10.3 GW at March 31, 2026, 100% TOPCon; module utilisation 43% for FY26, affected by Units 5 and 6 running only part-year. Q4 module production about 953 MW per management in Q&A, and G12R modules now in production.

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 2.94 GW; utilisation 69.9% in FY26 (43.3% in FY25), 79% in Q4 and about 85% in March 2026. Management expects a transition from M10 to G12R cells by end of the current quarter.

guidance_outlook: 6 GW integrated cell and module facility at Devanahalli: module line commissioning expected by end of calendar 2026, cell line by end of FY27.
Post-expansion installed capacity targeted at 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end of FY27.
Ingot and wafer facility of about 9 GW in phases: Phase 1 5 GW, Phase 2 4 GW a year later; first facility planned in FY29. Capex guided at INR 600-700 crore per GW.
Next-quarter DCR mix guided at 30-35% of module sales; by around the beginning of FY28 management expects nearly all sold capacity to be DCR.

544609|2026-09.headline: Physicswallah Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR1,242 crores, a record, with Pre-Ind AS EBITDA of INR233 crores at an 18.8% margin.
544609|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR1,242 crores (+18% YoY), with online up 26% to INR694 crores and offline up 9% to INR541 crores. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 45% to INR233 crores (18.8% margin, +350 bps), and PAT was INR142 crores versus INR70 crores a year earlier, taking H1 PAT to INR55 crores from a loss. NEET demand, delayed by a month, recovered only partly in Q2, and government-exam enrollments fell 24%, which weighed on offline and subsidiary Xylem. Management kept full-year consolidated revenue guidance of around 30% and said M&A is included in that figure. The company also sold its FinZ loan book and acquired an 11% stake in Sarrthi IAS.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record Q2, PAT turnaround and the held 30% and 100% EBITDA guides, but guarded on NEET recovery and on whether growth would exceed 30%; analysts pressed on how much collections must accelerate and on offline break-even.

544610|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 34% to INR 143 crore with 82.5% recurring; FY27 target INR 210 crore, with INR 190 crore visibility cited.
544610|2026-03.overview: Workmates reported FY26 revenue of INR 143 crore (up 34%) and PAT of INR 15.92 crore (up 16%, margin 11.1% vs 13%). Margins compressed: gross margin 32.8% vs 33.9% and EBITDA margin 16.2% vs 17.7%, which management attributes to a Dubai contract exit (about INR 4 crore), a gaming client exit (INR 3.5 crore) and about INR 6 crore of added headcount cost. Management set an FY27 revenue target of INR 210 crore (45%+ growth) and entered FY27 with MRR of INR 13.5 crore per month. This was the company's first earnings call since its BSE SME listing.

financial_highlights.value: INR 218 crore as stated on call (inconsistent with 82.5% recurring share of INR 143 crore revenue)

financial_highlights.change: +16% YoY; vs INR 13.9 crore (13%) in FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR 7.58 crore at FY26 entry; INR 10 crore at FY26 exit; INR 13.5 crore at FY27 opening
financial_highlights.change: FY27 opening is 35% above FY26 exit

segments.name: Recurring / annuity services
segments.commentary: Management said 82.5% of FY26 revenue was recurring; contracted recurring base of about INR 40 crore per quarter (about INR 160 crore annualised) for FY27.

segments.name: Project implementation (transformation)
segments.commentary: Project implementation billing grew 56.3% to INR 25 crore in FY26, described as the feeder for future managed services. H1 FY27 project billing visibility is about INR 5.82 crore.

segments.name: AI services
segments.commentary: AI services revenue was about INR 2 crore of the INR 143 crore in FY26; AI plus cybersecurity targeted at about 5% of FY27 revenue. Management says AI influences much larger cloud and managed services revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR 210 crore (45%+ growth); contracted/visible base INR 190.56 crore, leaving about INR 19-20 crore of new business to win over ~10 months.
H1 FY27 outlook about INR 91.56 crore (about INR 79-80 crore contracted, INR 6.15 crore recurring new, INR 5.82 crore project implementation); H2 estimate about INR 99 crore.
FY27 PAT guided at about INR 24-25 crore on INR 210 crore revenue; management said PAT margin would be similar to or higher than FY26 margin.
Margin recovery levers: higher AI and security mix, billable utilisation from 84% toward 88%, and operating leverage as new hires reach full productivity.
FY27 target excludes any US or UK turnover. AI expected to be a meaningful contributor in FY27 and the primary growth engine from FY28.
capex_capacity: Manpower cost about INR 16.9-17 crore on about 170 employees (about INR 9-10 lakh per head); FY27 existing-staff cost expected to rise to INR 18.5-19 crore with appraisals plus about INR 1.5 crore of new hires.
Three delivery centres (Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Hyderabad); nine locations in total. 120+ AWS-certified professionals out of 170+ staff.

US billing entity setup initiated; full US office and Singapore expansion contingent on geopolitical situation. Management said a light, fractional-consultant model will be used for global acquisition.
IntelliOps AI operations platform onboarded for more than 60% (later stated 65-70%) of customers; management intends to list it on the AWS marketplace.
demand_pricing: Management described competition as spanning TCS, Infosys and Accenture, Big Four firms, and mid-size cloud peers such as Minfy and Rapyder. Differentiators cited: AWS premier-tier partner status (less than 1% of AWS partners globally), Gen-AI competency, and the highest count of AWS competencies in India.

Pipeline includes Agentic AI platform migration, Gen-AI and data analytics in manufacturing, AI-led transformation for a large insurer, fintech cloud migrations and an NBFC cloud implementation. Management said 7-8 enterprise deals were targeted for closure in Q2.
Enterprise client count rose from 34 to 38; 28 net new clients added; top 20 accounts contributed 73% of revenue; client retention 95%. Management said top-5 concentration has declined.

Management said customers negotiate hard on managed-services and implementation pricing in India, while accepting AWS consumption costs. Hardware prices reportedly doubled or tripled, which management views as a tailwind for cloud migration.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of the INR 210 crore FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Anirban Dasgupta said about INR 160 crore is contracted (INR 40 crore per quarter), plus INR 30 crore visibility, giving INR 190.56 crore; the remaining about INR 19 crore must be won over 10 months.

qa_highlights.question: What PAT margin is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasish Sarkar said PAT margin would be around the same or higher, equating to about INR 24-25 crore PAT on INR 210 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will manpower cost rise as revenue scales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bulk of practice investments are done; existing staff cost goes to about INR 18.5-19 crore with appraisals plus about INR 1.5 crore of new hires. AI tools are expected to let the same headcount deliver more projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is there hardware or GPU cost pass-through risk on annuity contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Anirban Dasgupta said AWS prices have stayed flat or fallen, the platform provides GPU and LLM infrastructure via Bedrock, and there is no cost surprise in existing revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI revenue share and is it linked to cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 pure AI services revenue was about INR 2 crore; AI plus cybersecurity targeted at about 5% of FY27 revenue; AI typically pulls through cloud and managed services.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Dubai contract declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamal Nath said credit-insurance checks failed for the customer and the replacement entity; the INR 1 crore per month order (about INR 12 crore) was declined on bad-debt risk.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility gap: about INR 19-20 crore of new book-and-bill must be won within about 10 months to reach INR 210 crore.
Margin compression in FY26 (gross margin down 110 bps, EBITDA down 150 bps); FY27 recovery depends on utilisation rising from 84% to 88% and new hires reaching productivity.

AI will be a meaningful contributor in FY27, and our primary growth engine from FY28 onwards.

544610|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 27.5% YoY to INR 95.21 crore; FY27 outlook raised to INR 202 crore from INR 190.56 crore.
544610|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 95.21 crore, up 27.5% YoY, with recurring revenue up 43% to INR 82.97 crore (87% of revenue). PAT grew 32.4% to INR 12.03 crore, but operating cash flow was negative INR 4.7 crore as receivables rose to INR 39.5 crore. Management raised FY27 revenue outlook to INR 202 crore, leaving a gap of under INR 8 crore to the INR 210 crore goal. International expansion (US subsidiary registered, Middle East and Singapore go-to-market recalibrated) was triggered.

segments.name: Recurring / annuity
segments.commentary: INR 82.97 crore in H1, up 43% YoY; average MRR INR 13.5 crore vs INR 9.67 crore in H1 FY26. Gross churn annualised 2.6% against a 10% internal ceiling.

segments.name: Projects
segments.commentary: INR 12.24 crore in H1, below a strong H1 FY26 but 51% above H2 FY26. Management described project billing as cyclical.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Financial services is the largest vertical at about 41% of revenue. Top 20 clients are 71% of revenue, down from 73%.

segments.name: AI and cybersecurity
segments.commentary: Contributes about 5% of revenue. Six accelerators are in live production with clients.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue outlook raised to INR 202 crore from INR 190.56 crore; INR 210 crore goal now short by under INR 8 crore.
H2 estimate of INR 107 crore: INR 95.4 crore contracted recurring, INR 1.25 crore new recurring, INR 10.35 crore projects.

Weighted H2 pipeline of about INR 110 crore, including a large cloud migration for an existing NBFC client, a significant cybersecurity opportunity and a large migration for a mid-sized global IT services firm.
Management reiterated full-year PAT ambition of INR 24-25 crore; H1 PAT of INR 12.03 crore is in line with that.
Four H2 priorities: convert pipeline, start US and Middle East operations, reduce debtor days, convert profit into cash.
Billable utilisation at 84%, with a target of 88%.
capex_capacity: H1 capex INR 2.36 crore, mainly AI accelerator build cost; accelerators capitalised as intangible assets and amortised over five years.

Headcount flat at 169 (168 a year earlier); revenue per employee rose to INR 56.56 crore for the half (figure as stated in the call; appears to be an annualised or unit error versus the INR 0.44 crore prior-year figure).
Hiring planned for skill gaps and senior resources and for sales and customer-facing roles in new territories; not expected to scale linearly with revenue.
US subsidiary registered; billing awaits remaining registration steps and intimation to exchanges. Singapore subsidiary already operational with active AWS and Zoho customers.
Delivery is from Indian centres; Bhubaneswar stock used for managed security services.
demand_pricing: Management says AWS has not raised prices on any service in several years and has not seen GPU price increases despite AWS capacity-constraint comments.
AWS consumption margins vary by type: 8-12% typical, 18-20% for large migrations, higher under MAP 2.0 programmes. AI and analytics projects earn more than vanilla compute.
AWS payment terms: Workmates pays AWS in 30 days; customers pay in 45-60 days.
Cloud consumption (third-party cost) rose 72 bps to 66.5% of revenue, which drove the YoY gross margin dip.
Marketplace revenue is very small at present.
No live contract yet with large system integrators or GCCs; discussions ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: How much recurring revenue comes from pass-through AWS consumption, and does it include security and value-added services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AWS consumption is about 83% of the INR 95 crore, with services about 17.5%. Security and AI services are blended across managed services and project buckets.

qa_highlights.question: Has AWS capacity constraints or memory costs affected pricing, discounts, credits or GPU/Bedrock availability?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact so far. Management said AWS has not raised prices and expects higher demand to lift consumption and indirect implementation revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the accelerators' revenue contribution, monetisation and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: AI and cybersecurity are about 5% of revenue. Management cited 8-10 live opportunities for VoxoRA and VerID, and about seven or eight CloudTrustmate customers onboarded. No margin or revenue target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did project revenue fall about 27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Project revenue is cyclical and depends on completions. H1 FY26 included long-running projects that completed then. H1 FY27 billing was about INR 12 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Singapore, US and Middle East subsidiaries start operations?
qa_highlights.answer: Singapore is operational with customers added in H1. US registration is partly complete, with a few steps left before billing. Management did not give a Middle East timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company debt-free and does it plan debt or acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt planned. Management is open to complementary acquisitions in AI, cybersecurity and analytics, or partnerships in the US and Middle East. Management said there are no current foreign talks.

International expansion carries early-stage execution risk; Singapore go-to-market was recalibrated with no write-off stated.
Top 20 client concentration at 71% of revenue; AWS dependence (single-hyperscaler focus).

544612|2026-03.headline: FY26 value added revenue rose 12.3% to INR49,180 million with a record 18.8% EBITDA margin; Q4 EBITDA up 17.6% to INR2,573 million.
544612|2026-03.overview: Management reported its best full year yet: FY26 VAR grew 12.3% to INR49,180 million, EBITDA rose 13.5% to INR9,255 million, and EBITDA margin reached a record 18.8% of VAR. Q4 VAR grew 17.5% to INR14,058 million, with EBITDA margin stable at 18.3% despite geopolitical cost pressures. Advanced Ride Technologies drove growth (FY26 up 19.7%), while Clean Air and Powertrain grew only 5.5% for the year. Lifetime order book stood at INR124,000 million at March 31, 2026, with exports and new Clean Air and bearings wins cited as growth drivers.

segments.name: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,296 million, up 5.5% YoY; Q4 INR6,905 million, up 9.9%. Growth tepid due to OEM and within-OEM mix shifts (lower-end SUVs, EV mix at a European OEM), not share loss per management.

segments.name: Advanced Ride Technologies (suspension)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,885 million, up 19.7% YoY; Q4 INR7,153 million, up 26%. DCx DaVinci mechanical suspension adopted by a leading Indian OEM for a flagship SUV.

guidance_outlook: Lifetime order book of INR124,000 million gives 100% visibility of FY2028 internal revenue target; management expects double-digit medium-term growth.
Export order book expected to keep growing; current exports are about 5-6% of sales versus a 14-20% share of the order book (as stated).
New West India shock absorber plant (board-approved) expected to take 6-12 months to commission; peak revenue contribution expected mid-2028 to 2029.
Clean Air entry into the largest Indian PV OEM's supplier panel for a Gasoline Particulate Filter; growth expected from late FY27/FY28.
Management expects margins to remain stable going forward.
Addressable Clean Air content from CAFE 3 and BS7 estimated at INR1,300-1,400 crore over the next three to five years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex of about INR1,400 million across the North India Clean Air facility (announced Q3 FY26) and a new greenfield West India Advanced Ride Technologies plant.
FY26 capex was about INR1,150 million.
Bearings business: new plant not yet decided; management is checking whether existing plants can accommodate the new bearings business.
Capex-to-steady-state revenue ratio cited as roughly 1:3.
Localization about 89-90%, management intends to keep it near 90% over the long term.
demand_pricing: Management says the DCx DaVinci suspension has 3-4 OEMs interested, including Indian, Japanese, Korean and European OEMs; it targets about 50% of India's roughly 5-5.5 million PV market.
Conventional mechanical dampers still dominate over 90% of Indian passenger vehicles.
Export drivers cited: technology equalization (BS6.2 with RDE, Euro 6 RDE), China-plus-one sourcing, labour cost advantage and rupee depreciation.

Direct material cost (steel) recovered through quarterly escalator agreements; indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, fuel) being recovered through customer negotiations, which management says can be tough.
Management said currency depreciation gives an immediate 15-20% improvement in global competitiveness.

qa_highlights.question: How will exports ramp over the next two to three years, and when will the new plants and bearings orders commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are described as middle-ended, with a critical mass around 2028 and ramp starting 2027-28. The West India plant takes 6-12 months to commission; peak around mid-2028 to 2029. Bearings value not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is content per vehicle for commercial vehicle exhaust systems versus passenger vehicles, and how do diesel, petrol, CNG and hybrid differ?
qa_highlights.answer: A commercial exhaust is 3-4x a passenger car system and can reach 10x for tractors with aftertreatment. Diesel carries higher hot-end content. Hybrids can lift content from 1x to 1.5-2x. CNG and hybrid need exhaust systems with no content loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports go directly to third-party OEMs or only to Tenneco group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports go both to Tenneco group entities and to third-party OEMs with group permission, which management frames as partnership, not competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why no two-wheeler suspension or Clean Air two-wheeler presence, and is the CV localization point about Clean Air?
qa_highlights.answer: Management avoids low-margin two- and three-wheelers and will enter only with technology differentiation; M&A also being considered. The CV localization reference relates to Clean Air, with localization about 89-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Clean Air growth tepid and what drives the margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was held back by absence from the largest PV OEM and by mix shifts at existing OEMs. Margins attributed to the P3 operating model, standardized Lego-brick product design, and a higher-margin export order book; management expects margins to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: How do OEMs upgrade from passive to passive-plus or DaVinci suspension, and what is the cost delta?
qa_highlights.answer: Upgrades within mechanical suspension fit the existing packaging envelope with small cost delta. Electronics and software (semi-active CVSA) above about INR35 lakh MSRP need routing and ECU changes, which raise cost substantially.

qa_highlights.question: How are currency movements and indirect cost inflation handled in export contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Currency depreciation is seen as a benefit. Indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, LPG, CNG, crude) are being bundled and recovered from customers, with cost-cutting in SG&A and factory efficiency as mitigation.

risks_watch: Clean Air growth lagged the market in FY26 due to OEM mix shifts and absence from the largest PV OEM until FY28.

544612|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.2% YoY to INR15,448 million; VAR up 18.4% to INR13,816 million, EBITDA margin 17.9% of VAR.
544612|2026-06.overview: Tenneco Clean Air India reported Q1 FY27 value added revenue (VAR) of INR13,816 million, up 18.4% YoY, with ART growing 27.9% and Clean Air and Powertrain growing 9.6%. EBITDA rose 7.9% YoY to INR2,469 million, with margin at 17.9% of VAR, down about 170 bps YoY and 43 bps QoQ as commodity inflation, rupee depreciation, Middle East-related costs and listed-company costs weighed. 544614|2026-06.headline: Capillary Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to INR256 crore and adjusted EBITDA to INR44 crore (~17%), with organic growth at 17%.
544614|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR256 crore, up 43% YoY, with two months of SessionM (acquired May 1, 2026) contributing; organic growth was 17% and currency added about 6%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR44 crore (about 17-18% margin) versus INR19 crore a year earlier, and reported PAT was -INR9.5 crore, or INR25 crore normalised after excluding a cyber-fraud loss and a one-time deferred tax charge. ARR reached INR1,026 crore (+34% YoY), and trailing-12-month new ACV excluding one large healthcare win was about INR92 crore (+75%). Management kept FY27 guidance of INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA unchanged, saying it expects to beat both.

financial_highlights.change: +132% YoY; from INR19 crore; organic EBITDA margin ~23%
Includes cyber-fraud exceptional loss and one-time deferred tax liability
Up from INR19 crore in Q4 FY26
+34% YoY; from INR765 crore in FY26 and INR608 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Trailing-12-month new ACV (ex one healthcare win)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR17 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Loyalty stack
segments.commentary: Over 90% of revenue; core product and the business's main monetisation layer. Contracts are typically 3-7 year subscriptions.

segments.name: Engage (Engage+)
segments.commentary: About 5% of revenue; one-to-one personalised customer communication platform.

segments.name: Rewards
segments.commentary: About 5-7% of revenue; mainly banks and telcos.

segments.name: aiRA (AI analytics and action agents)
segments.commentary: About USD2.5 million ARR (~26 customers live, under 10 paying); management targets 5-10% of revenue from aiRA in FY27. Gross margin above 80%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged at INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA; management expects to beat both but did not quantify.
Organic growth expected at about 17% for FY27 (about 20-23% including FX and inorganic); management described 15-20% as the organic run-rate.
Kognitiv: first customer migration to go live September 1, 2026; ~16-17 customers in total; migration of the full base targeted by September 2027, with ~INR15-20 crore EBITDA uplift from Kognitiv.

SessionM: management expects EBITDA margin to move from break-even to ~15% within a year and to 35-40% over a further year; server cost savings of USD6-8 million over 3-4 quarters, with a payback possibly within FY27.
ESOP expense guided at INR12-15 crore for FY27, kept at 1-2% of revenue.
New ACV expected to grow at least 30-40% YoY in FY27 (not the 75% trailing figure).
capex_capacity: SessionM acquired from Mastercard effective May 1, 2026; enterprise value USD20 million, net cost about INR17 crore after net-debt true-up on April 30; entities debt-free; SessionM ARR about USD32 million, all contracts agreed to move to Capillary paper.
Kognitiv (closed May 1, 2025): ~16-17 customers; AI-led migration tool; first customer live Sept 1, 2026.
Migration of SessionM customers not expected to start until end-2026 / early 2027; 3-4 of ~45 SessionM customers are being fast-tracked.
Cloud-native platform across four colos; product uptime of nearly 5 nines in Q1.
CustomerGlu tuck-in (rebranded Experiences+) bought for less than a few hundred thousand dollars; acqui-hire IP deal.
demand_pricing: Win rates on large new deals above 35%, which management attributes partly to aiRA.
Existing-customer NRR of 111% split roughly: 4-5% from price escalators and overages, ~10% from upsell and new cohorts, net of ~5% churn.
Management frames loyalty as a red ocean; about 90 loyalty companies have revenue of USD10-100 million and are the M&A pool.
Acquired agency-model businesses run at ~30% gross margin; moving them onto the platform lifts gross margin to 65-75%.
Management says fewer than 10% of loyalty revenue sits with software vendors versus agencies; named competitors include Epsilon, Merkle, Kobie and Salesforce.

qa_highlights.question: What share of SessionM clients have migrated and what is the FY27 run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: No SessionM migrations before end-2026/early 2027; the full base is expected to take 2-3 years. 3-4 of ~45 customers are being fast-tracked; margins will improve through server cost cuts (SessionM server costs are ~50% of revenue vs ~7-9% at Capillary).

qa_highlights.question: Organic vs inorganic growth split and FX effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 organic growth was 17%; FX contributed about 6%; the rest is SessionM's two months. Cash is about half USD and half INR, which gives a natural hedge with the US at ~60% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cyber-fraud loss covered by insurance?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the bank-account fraud at a subsidiary is insured, but the amount and timing of recovery are not yet clear. No customer or employee data was exposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic NRR breakdown and churn?
qa_highlights.answer: Price escalators and overage are 4-5% of NRR; upsell and new cohorts add ~10%; churn is ~5%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the aiRA figures net of cannibalisation and what are the economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ARR is ~USD2.5 million with no cannibalisation so far; gross and contribution margins are above 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the SessionM purchase price INR17 crore when the deal was USD20 million?
qa_highlights.answer: The USD20 million enterprise value was adjusted for net debt at closing; the final true-up on April 30 brought the value to about INR17 crore; the entities are debt-free.

risks_watch: Q1 organic NRR excluding the healthcare account was 116%, but reported 111%; one large healthcare customer did not grow, which weighs on the quarter.
Enterprise budget cycles and ~9-month average deal cycles make quarterly new ACV lumpy (trailing-12-month metric).
Kognitiv migration milestone on September 1, 2026 is the first test of the AI-led upgrade approach; success is needed for the INR15-20 crore EBITDA uplift.
Reported PAT is negative; the insurance recovery on the fraud loss is still uncertain.
aiRA is early: under 10 of ~26 live customers are paying, and the 5-10% revenue target depends on enterprise budget timing.
key_quotes: We will definitely beat our INR1,065 crores and revenue and INR172 crores number. I don't think we want to revise any guidance right now.
So, we will not start any SessionM migrations till probably end of this year, early next year, right.
Yes, so we are right now, I would say at like $2 million, $2.5 million in terms of revenue run rates on aiRA.
So, it's a it is going to be a big driver on the NRR side going forward as well.
But how much and when it would be recovered, I think that we don't have clarity on, so that work is in progress at this point in time.
544614|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, AI product adoption and the SessionM and Kognitiv integration plans, and firm on keeping FY27 guidance unchanged while expecting to beat it. Management was more cautious on timing: SessionM migrations are not expected before end-2026, insurance recovery of the cyber-fraud loss is unclear, and the Q1 organic growth was partly weighed by one large healthcare customer.

rows.why: SessionM EBITDA guided from break-even to ~15% within a year and to 35-40% over a further year, with USD6-8 million server cost savings over 3-4 quarters; Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin was ~17-18% versus ~23% organic, and Kognitiv targets INR15-20 crore EBITDA uplift.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic growth guided at ~17% for FY27 (15-20% run-rate), ARR INR1,026 crore (+34%), and NRR 111% (116% ex one healthcare account) with ~10% from upsell and new cohorts.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it expects to beat INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA but did not quantify; ARR of INR1,026 crore (+34% YoY) and win rates above 35% back the claim.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA and said it will definitely beat both; Q1 revenue of INR256 crore (+43%, organic +17%) and adjusted EBITDA of INR44 crore (~17-18% margin) support the run-rate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Kognitiv AI-led migration first customer goes live Sept 1, 2026, with ~16-17 customers and full base upgrades by Sept 2027; aiRA targets 5-10% of FY27 revenue from ~USD2.5 million ARR with ~26 customers live.

rows.label: New ACV growth 30-40% in FY27
rows.why: Management expects new ACV to grow at least 30-40% YoY in FY27 versus the trailing ~INR92 crore (+75%), which is a lower bar than the trailing figure but still implies FY27 new ACV of roughly INR120-130 crore if the base is ~INR92 crore.

rows.label: SessionM server cost cuts
rows.why: SessionM server costs are ~50% of revenue versus ~7-9% at Capillary, and management guides USD6-8 million of server savings with payback possibly within FY27.

rows.label: SessionM migration to Capillary platform
rows.when: not before end-2026 / early 2027; full base 2-3 years
rows.why: Only 3-4 of ~45 SessionM customers are fast-tracked, so migration-driven margin gains are mostly outside the next 2-4 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, aiRA adoption, win rates above 35% and reiterating FY27 guidance with an expected beat, but cautious on SessionM migration timing (not before end-2026), the uncertain insurance recovery on the cyber-fraud loss, and one large healthcare customer weighing on organic

544617|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹812 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 30.3% from 40.5% on a ₹85 mn-per-quarter US near-shore team cost booked in other expenses.
544617|2026-03.overview: Excelsoft reported Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹812 mn (up 16% YoY) and FY26 revenue of ₹2,725 mn (down from the ₹3,333 mn stated for FY25, although management described FY26 growth as 17%). Q4 EBITDA fell 13% YoY to ₹246 mn and PAT fell to ₹166 mn from ₹205 mn, as other expenses rose 76% to ₹209 mn on a 30-person US near-shore consultant team hired from January. Management said the cost is a one-off that will lift margins back to about 30-31%, and it flagged a planned UK awarding-body (AQA) announcement and a renewed acquisition push under new CEO Doreswamy Palaniswamy.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹205 mn in Q4 FY25; PAT margin 20.5% vs 29.3%
stated as 17% growth vs ₹3,333 mn in FY25
+25% vs ₹347 mn, driven by lower tax; PAT margin 16%
useful life of products ~10 years (5-10 years cited)
technology services ~₹175 cr; excludes existing-customer expansion and new wins

segments.name: Educational technology services (ETS)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew about 37% YoY (up ₹117 mn) and share was 54% in Q4 and 56% in FY26. ETS services gross margin is about 56%, per management.

segments.name: Assessment and proctoring solutions (A&P)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of ₹744 mn, up 18%; share was 29% in Q4 and 27% in FY26. Management did not give a test-volume figure on the call.

segments.name: Learning and student success solutions
segments.commentary: Contributed 14% of Q4 revenue and 12% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Learning design and content solutions
segments.commentary: Contributed 3% of Q4 revenue and 5% of FY26 revenue; a new US engagement with an online course content provider was won in the year.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North America was 62.7% of Q4 revenue and 64.9% of FY26 revenue. Europe and UK was 25.4% in Q4 and 22.7% in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margins to return to the normal range of about 30-31% once the US near-shore team cost is absorbed (said in response to an analyst question).
Management expects to return to organic growth of about 20-25% overall.
The AQA (UK awarding body) engagement is said to have started on the basis of a 1 March LOI; a larger AQA announcement was said to be due within one to two days of the call.
The US near-shore team's gross margin is currently about 30%, and management expects it to move toward roughly 54-56% as other services business is scaled.

Management is pursuing inorganic opportunities, including overseas acquisitions in the US, and says the acquisition strategy is 'intact and in progress', with new CEO Doreswamy Palaniswamy now leading it.
Management plans to reduce capitalised product development over time and expense more of it, and says the ratio of intangible investment to revenue is declining.
capex_capacity: Around 30 professionals hired in January 2026 as consultants for a US near-shore services team, at a cost of about ₹8.5 cr per quarter (about ₹34 cr annualised), expensed in other expenses.
AI R&D team of about 45 people with NVIDIA GPU laptops and data-center GPUs, plus edge compute (NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi) testing.
AI-enabled infrastructure is being built at the network edge and in Excelsoft's own secure data centres rather than relying wholly on public cloud.
Intangible assets capitalised were ₹12.2 cr in FY26, with cumulative book value of about ₹100 cr and annual amortisation of about ₹18 cr.
Three additional senior sales hires in the US, one in the Middle East and one in the UK, plus a few in India; two senior marketing and business development consultants engaged.
demand_pricing: Management said it has not lost a client and that the top 10 clients have an average tenure of about 11 years. Top 5 clients were about 68% of FY26 revenue and top 10 about 78%.
Added 14 new clients in FY26. Pipeline is focused on education, certification, publishing and public sector.

New wins include a multi-year VTCT Skills engagement (about 300,000 vocational and technical exams a year), the Civil Service Commission of the Philippines, and an UK engagement with a large examination body, with rollout over three years. Other UK vocational partners named include AQA, TQUK, VTCT and CQI.
April 2026 revenue was about ₹23 cr against about ₹15 cr in April 2025, which management linked partly to new business from the near-shore team.
Management said handwritten-script digitisation (AI text extraction and e-marking) is a new business line; one customer accounts for about 12 million answer scripts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~₹8.4-8.5 cr quarterly near-shore expense one-off or recurring, and why is it in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the team of about 30 is a fixed cost that will recur at about ₹8.5 cr a quarter but will not grow further. Consultants were used for legal reasons and the cost sits in other expenses because they are not on payroll; lock-ins are in place.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential and margin of the 30-member US team?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is at least 15% above the team's cost. Gross margin is about 30% currently, against about 56% for typical technology services, and is expected to converge as offshore and near-shore work combine.

qa_highlights.question: What is the confirmed order backlog, split between ETS and A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the order book, including confirmed and expected, is just over ₹300 cr and executable, of which technology services is about ₹175 cr. It excludes expansion of existing customers and new wins.

qa_highlights.question: How many A&P tests were conducted in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure and said it would announce a break-up of test types (formative, high-stakes, proctored and non-proctored) later.

qa_highlights.question: Who is the new CEO and what will he change?
qa_highlights.answer: Doreswamy Palaniswamy is a Chartered Accountant with about 25 years of experience, including CFO and COO roles and about 13-14 acquisitions. He will set direction, focus on platformisation and acquisitions, and rely on the existing team.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the acquisition process, which has been paused for about six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the strategy is intact. Work was paused until the new CEO reviewed it, and due diligence is being refreshed and is progressing significantly.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the US near-shore team converting into business, and its gross margin is currently about 30% against a company norm of about 56%.

Q4 PAT fell 19% YoY and FY26 EBITDA was flat, while the reported FY26 figures imply a decline in revenue versus FY25 (₹2,725 mn vs ₹3,333 mn), so the reconciliation of the growth figures needs checking.
The AQA announcement and its revenue size were still pending at the time of the call, and management declined to quantify it.
Acquisition timing is uncertain, with spending on diligence and a paused process before the new CEO's review.
Intangible capitalisation (₹12.2 cr in FY26; cumulative ~₹100 cr; amortisation ~₹18 cr a year) will be a recurring D&A and profit-quality item to track.
Concentration risk: top 5 clients are about 68% of revenue.
544617|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and order visibility, but defensive and evasive on specifics: the near-shore cost was framed as a one-off even though it recurs quarterly, and A&P test volumes and AQA size were deferred to future announcements.
key_quotes: That means a direct attributable expense of 85 million in Q4 towards establishing this team is part of other expenses because they were hired as consultants.
This was pretty much one-off where the margin was shrunk because of this expense.
The fact that we have not lost a client but we are able to do more with clients from last year gives us a competitive edge in the marketplace.
So the acquisition strategy is intact and in progress.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides normalised EBITDA margin back to 30-31% from 30.3% in Q4 FY26, but the ~Rs8.5 cr/quarter near-shore team cost recurs (it is not one-off) and the team's gross margin is only ~30% vs ~56% norm, so recovery depends on converting that team into business.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: A 30-person US near-shore team was hired in Jan 2026 (already commissioned) and 3 US, 1 Middle East, 1 UK senior sales hires are planned, but no capacity numbers or timing were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides to a return to 20-25% organic growth, backed by a ~Rs300 cr executable order book (~Rs175 cr tech services), 14 new clients added in FY26 and April 2026 revenue of Rs23 cr vs Rs15 cr; Q4 revenue grew 16% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond ~Rs12.2 cr of capitalised intangibles in FY26 and management plans to reduce capitalised product development over time, so a new capex programme is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on growth and order visibility and has a larger AQA announcement due within 1-2 days of the call, but no quantified upgrade was given and the AQA size was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Near-shore team costs of ~Rs8.5 cr/quarter recur while its gross margin is ~30%, and FY26 revenue reconciliation is unclear (Rs2,725 mn vs Rs3,333 mn in FY25 despite stated 17% growth), so margin guidance could slip if the team does not convert.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Handwritten-script digitisation (AI text extraction and e-marking) is described as a new business line with one customer at ~12 mn answer scripts, and AI R&D team of ~45 people is working on products.

rows.label: UK AQA awarding-body engagement and larger announcement
rows.when: within 1-2 days of the call, then next 2-4 quarters
rows.why: AQA engagement started on a 1 March LOI and a larger announcement was said to be due within one to two days of the call, though management declined to quantify its revenue size.

rows.label: Overseas (US) acquisitions under new CEO
rows.why: Management says the acquisition strategy is 'intact and in progress' with due diligence refreshed and progressing significantly after a ~six-month pause, but timing is uncertain and no deal is named.

rows.label: Lower capitalised product development, more expensed
rows.why: Management plans to reduce capitalised product development over time, while capitalised intangibles were Rs12.2 cr in FY26 against ~Rs18 cr annual amortisation, so profit quality and D&A will be tracked.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, order visibility and the acquisition push, but defensive on the near-shore cost (framed as one-off though it recurs at ~Rs8.5 cr/quarter) and evasive on A&P test volumes and AQA size; analysts pressed on the cost and its treatment in other expenses.

544617|2026-06.headline: Excelsoft Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44.05% YoY to INR802.63 million, while EBITDA margin fell to 16.24% from 18.02%.
544617|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 44.05% YoY to INR802.63 million, led by the education technology services (ETS) business, which grew 177% YoY. EBITDA rose 29.78% to INR130.31 million, but margin contracted about 178 bps to 16.24% due to nearshore build-out, international sales hiring, one-time recruitment and AI training costs. PAT rose 57.13% to INR92.28 million, helped by lower interest cost. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR350-360 crore and year-end EBITDA margin of 24-25%.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR7.8 million last year (per Q&A)
Management expects to normalise to last year's level or slightly lower by year-end

segments.name: Education technology services (ETS)
segments.commentary: Approximately 63.4% of Q1 revenue; grew 177% YoY, driven by large engagements and nearshore expansion. Management attributed Q4 US onsite placements to wins now showing in Q1.

segments.name: Assessment and proctoring solutions
segments.commentary: Approximately 23.5% of revenue. Management said product revenue was roughly flat YoY in Q1 and guided 25-30% product growth for the full year.

segments.name: Learning and student success; learning design services
segments.commentary: Remaining revenue share, described as stable contributors; no separate figures given.

segments.name: Nearshore operations
segments.commentary: About INR10 crore revenue in Q1 at about 26% gross margin, up from single digits at inception; nearly INR40 crore secured for FY27 and 35-40% gross margin targeted over time.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR350-360 crore; management said it is confident of about INR350 crore and could stretch closer, but would not commit to INR400 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25%; management said it would rather deliver a higher top line at about 25% margin than grow 20-25% at 27-30% margin.
Management said 30%-plus revenue growth is targeted; Q1 is typically 20-22% of annual revenue.
AQA: about USD17 million revenue visibility over four years, with about INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 and INR12-15 crore billing expected in FY27; no quantified contribution in FY28.
Long-term growth mix of roughly 69-70% organic and 30% inorganic over the next five years, per management.
Product revenue expected to grow 25-30% for the full year, with Q1 seasonally low on test volumes.
capex_capacity: Fresh capitalization about INR4 crore in Q1 for AI-native products; management said investment was front-loaded and would normalise to last year's level or slightly lower by year-end.
Nearshore delivery team being built; management said it will not add nearshore capacity beyond customer necessity.
Exploring a Toronto, Canada office to place US-facing staff for business development given visa difficulties.
Three acquisition targets in pipeline: one US, two India. Non-binding offers issued for two; one earlier target in final negotiation stage, with decision expected within a couple of weeks.
Cash and FDs of about INR400 crore; management described balance sheet as healthy.
demand_pricing: Top 5 customers about 70% of Q1 revenue; top 10 about 83%.
Nearshore team now serves 2 clients, up from 1 at start.
AQA engagement (GCSE e-marking) in pilot and phased deployment; described as second-largest account once it scales.
Management pursuing National Testing Agency-related opportunity after recent exam problems; met a government 4-member task force.
Expansion in US, UK and Dubai sales teams cited as driving pipeline and new logo wins; no pricing data disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins guided at 24-25% when earlier commentary implied 30-31% for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier view excluded sales hiring and internal capability costs. It chose a conservative 24-25% EBITDA target, with possible further AI-related investment, and expects faster top-line growth to offset percentage margin pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the one-time costs confined to FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth of 30%-plus needs investment, and further spend may be required, so it would not commit to margin recovery beyond 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 seasonally weakest, and what is the FY27 revenue number?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is typically 20-22% of annual revenue. Management guided INR350-360 crore, and said INR400 crore was not committed.

qa_highlights.question: How much AQA revenue is booked and what is the scale?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 with billing started; INR12-15 crore expected in FY27. Four-year visibility is roughly USD17 million, with upside.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Three targets: one US and two India. Non-binding offers issued for two; one is in final negotiation stage, with outcome expected in a couple of weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Will nearshore expansion compromise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there would be lower margins in the short term, but nearshore would be used to retain and win customers before shifting work offshore, and would not be built ahead of customer need.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT exceed EBIT by so much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management explained that other income sits below operating EBIT in the presentation and interest was the major item; interest was INR15.05 million vs INR7.8 million last year.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin contraction to 16.24% in Q1; FY27 guidance of 24-25% implies recovery in later quarters.
Interest expense nearly doubled to INR15.05 million YoY; watch debt and cost of funding.
High client concentration: top 5 customers 70% of revenue.
Product revenue flat YoY in Q1; 25-30% full-year growth requires a pick-up in test volumes.
Acquisition execution risk; one deal previously written off and renegotiated.
Ongoing AI upskilling spend may continue for about two years, per management.
AQA ramp depends on phased deployment; no FY28 contribution quantified.
544617|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and pipeline, but cautious and conservative on margins: management repeatedly chose to guide to 24-25% EBITDA and said it would 'deliver more probably.' Answers on acquisitions, AQA and the Q&A on product growth were sometimes vague or unquantified.
key_quotes: We would want to take the first one, right? So, grow at a faster pace, so that we acquire the market quickly, and then grow to a, God forbid, let's say, God willing, a INR1,000 crores company earlier than anybody's normal imagination.
So we are in that direction and we are pretty much confident on achieving those numbers.

Doreswamy Palaniswamy: Sir, we would be, as we have kind of in the last quarter also we mentioned that we would be somewhere around like 24%, 25% on our margin, that's going to be the year end margin.
And that is a training that will go on, up-skilling that will go on for a couple of more years.
So we want to do is ensure that it would be a 25% for sure.
Excluding these one -time expenses, our operating margins remain broadly stable year -over-year, demonstrating the resilience of our core operating model.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin of 24-25% from a 16.24% Q1 base, which requires a steep recovery, and nearshore gross margin is about 26% today versus a 35-40% target over time.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nearshore delivery team is being built for 2 clients (up from 1), with nearly INR40 crore secured for FY27, but management will not add nearshore capacity beyond customer necessity and no capacity count is given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: ETS revenue grew 177% YoY to about 63.4% of Q1 revenue, product growth is guided at 25-30% for FY27 (Q1 product revenue roughly flat), and management targets 30%-plus revenue growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as a formal programme; fresh capitalisation is about INR4 crore in Q1 for AI-native products, expected to normalise to last year's level or slightly lower by year-end, and the Toronto office and acquisitions are still at exploration or negotiation stage, so no firm capex plan is in place.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it is confident of about INR350 crore and could stretch closer to the INR360 crore top end, but would not commit to INR400 crore; Q1 revenue grew 44.05% YoY to INR802.63 million.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to 16.24% from 18.02%, and FY27 guidance needs a recovery to 24-25%; management said further AI-related spend may be needed and interest cost nearly doubled to INR15.05 million, so the margin path carries execution risk even though revenue guidance is held at INR350-360 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AQA (GCSE e-marking) is in pilot and phased deployment with about INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 and INR12-15 crore billing expected in FY27; AI-native products are receiving investment.

rows.label: AQA contract ramp to INR12-15 crore FY27 billing
rows.why: About USD17 million over four years of visibility with INR2.5 crore booked in Q1 and INR12-15 crore billing expected in FY27, though no FY28 contribution is quantified.

rows.label: Acquisition decision on one target
rows.when: within a couple of weeks of the call
rows.why: One earlier target is in final negotiation with a decision expected in a couple of weeks; three targets in pipeline (one US, two India) with non-binding offers issued for two.

544617|2026-09.headline: Excelsoft Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.2% YoY to INR80.9 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.35% from 29.3% on overseas sales and talent investment.
544617|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 25.2% YoY to INR80.9 crore in Q2 FY27, and H1 revenue rose 33.9% to INR161.2 crore. EBITDA fell to INR13.2 crore (16.35% margin) from INR18.8 crore (29.3%), reflecting upfront spend on international sales, customer success and near-shore consultants. Management attributed part of the quarter's shortfall to revenue deferred into Q3 due to customer-side UAT, security clearances and billing delays, and said government-owned clients have slowed decision-making. Management guided to an EBITDA margin of 22-25% once the investments start yielding, and reiterated the INR350 crore FY27 revenue target.

qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed concentration is high but said the largest customer is multiple divisions with separate P&L owners, so the risk of losing many of them is remote. 544619|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 27.9% to INR642.3 crores and PAT to INR174.3 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 34.6% and working capital days rose to 213.
544619|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 27.9% YoY to INR642.3 crores, with EBITDA up 16.8% to INR221.9 crores and PAT up to INR174.3 crores from INR138.7 crores. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15.7% to INR182.3 crores, with EBITDA of INR62.6 crores at a 34.3% margin. Specialty ingredients grew 62% to INR280 crores and rose to 44% of revenue, while pharma, food and nutrition grew 10%. Working capital days increased from 184 to 213 on higher raw material and finished goods inventory, and management targets 150-160 days within FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about INR3 crores CSR spend, about INR1.5 crores of LPG premium costs in March, and about INR2 crores of air freight to the largest customer. These are expected to fall in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much battery material volume is expected in FY27?

qa_highlights.answer: Without incremental capex, the existing portfolio can scale to INR1,000-1,200 crores. Margin should recover toward the historical 24-25% (per the management answer), and bisglycinate should add higher-margin revenue from FY28.
