544619|2026-06.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 34.7% despite an LPG-driven specialty slowdown.
544619|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore and EBITDA rose 25% to INR54.9 crore, with margin at 34.7%. PAT increased to INR40.6 crore (PAT margin 25.6%). Pharma, food and nutrition (PFN) grew 31% (management also cited 30% in Q&A), mainly on volume from phosphates. Specialty ingredients grew 19% after LPG shortages in April and first half of May cut utilisation, and NSS (European subsidiary) was weak due to energy costs at a major infant formula customer in Ireland. Management said specialty and PFN momentum should continue into Q2, with price pass-through on phosphates mainly landing in Q2.

rows.why: PFN grew 31% YoY (about 3% from currency) on phosphate volume, phosphate demand exceeds current capacity, and specialty is expected to return to historical growth from Q2 after sub-50% utilisation in half of Q1.

rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, conditional on binding off-takes
rows.why: Scale-up from 100 to 200 KTPA is explicitly tied to two binding off-take agreements expected later in CY2026, and Dahej can support 200 KTPA; no new capex figure was given and management said immediate focus remains Phases 1-3.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No explicit revenue guidance was raised; NSS is guided flat to single-digit and management hedged on near-term margin recovery.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: LPG-driven specialty utilisation fell below 50% for half of Q1, NSS guided flattish to single-digit growth in FY27, and Bisglycinate deliveries are behind schedule, though phosphate price pass-through should land in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Greenfield Nandesari FDA approval expected in Q1 FY27 with supplies from Q3 FY27, and Bisglycinate has two large North American customers approved; Phase 2 HPMC/PVP excipients are not expected this financial year.

rows.label: Two binding SAM off-take agreements
rows.why: Two binding off-takes are expected later in CY2026 and gate the 100 to 200 KTPA scale-up, with 8 customers already qualified and 2 MOUs with South Korean cathode makers signed in Q1.

rows.label: Bisglycinate North American customer ramp
rows.why: Q1 Absorbis sales already exceed full FY26 sales and two large North American customers are approved, though deliveries are behind schedule and management expects a top 2-3 PFN product within 2-3 years.

rows.label: Working capital cycle normalisation
rows.when: medium term (near term ~170 days, long term ~150 days)
rows.why: Inventory was built for raw materials and battery business, with the near-term target around 170 days excluding battery and a long-term sustainable cycle near 150 days.

544619|2026-09.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR196.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 37.2%, a record quarter despite Fortified Rice pause.
544619|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with revenue up 21% YoY and 24% QoQ, and EBITDA margin up about 310 bps YoY to 37.2%. Pharma Food Nutrition (PFN) drove growth, rising 57% YoY, while Specialty Ingredients fell 25% YoY after the Government's Fortified Rice programme paused. PAT grew only 11% YoY to INR51.8 crore because of lower other income, a higher effective tax rate of 27%, and new greenfield depreciation. Management guided to positive YoY growth in Specialty Ingredients in Q3 and Q4 and kept the Dahej battery-materials start date of April 2027.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients

Magnesium bisglycinate targeted to become a top-3 PFN revenue contributor within 2-3 years, with potential of at least INR100 crore.

Binding offtake details for the battery business expected in the next call or within two months.

Existing Nandesari PFN site operating at close to optimum utilisation, about 80%. About 40% of Nandesari capacity is allocated to other products, and management expects 70-80% of that to go to magnesium bisglycinate.
Specialty Ingredients utilisation around 40-45% in FY26, expected to recover to about 40-45% by Q4 FY27.

Dahej battery plant: Phase 1 of 25,000 tpa commercial operations from April 2027; scale-up to 100,000 tpa and then 200,000 tpa. Management referred to about INR600 crore capex for the first 100,000 tpa.
FY27 capex about INR77 crore, mainly battery project at Dahej and greenfield completion. Battery inventory is being built up ahead of commissioning.
demand_pricing: Phosphoric acid prices rose about 40% vs Q4 FY26 by Q1 FY27 and strengthened further; pass-through was executed and Q1 inventory built ahead of price increases supported Q2 and October-November.
Management does not expect margins to strengthen further at current levels until the next contracting cycle.

Export share about 65% of revenue (exports up 24% YoY), domestic about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is Specialty Ingredients underlying growth excluding Fortified Rice, and what growth is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fortified Rice was about 20-25% of segment revenue (INR40-50 crore in FY26). Premix was hit by product mix change even though volumes grew. Non-Fortified Rice premix contracts for Q3 and Q4 are expected to largely offset the loss.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Specialty margin fall while PFN margins rose sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to operating leverage: premix, a large contributor, had limited revenue, and NSS was a drag. Q3 and Q4 contracts are expected to carry better margins than the Fortified Rice business they replace.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PFN growth from volume or pricing, and what is the PFN volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came mainly from phosphates (up about 70-80%) and magnesium bisglycinate, which received the maximum capacity allocation in the existing setup. PFN volume grew about 30-35% in Q2 and about 19% in H1.

qa_highlights.question: How will bisglycinate be distributed across customers, and how much of Nandesari capacity can go to it?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of bisglycinate volume will go to larger customers, including two of the largest US tolling manufacturers, and 50% to mid/small customers, to avoid concentration. About 70-80% of the 40% of capacity allocated to other products would go to bisglycinate; the remaining 60% of the greenfield is mainly phosphates and is not easily fungible.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Phase 1 battery capacity is covered by binding offtake agreements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give volume detail today, saying the company would break it out by customer and volume at the next call or within two months. Binding commitments are targeted for Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the battery pricing premium and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is set at a slight premium to China, driven by US 45X PFE-compliant supply rules, and capped by competitiveness. Management targets asset turns of about 3x and ROCE similar to the core business, and will not guide EBITDA margin for the battery business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Phase 1 plant approval needed for Korean customers, and how long does validation take?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant approval for the Dahej site is expected to take 3-6 months because product and process approval is already in place. Management assumes about half a year of FY28 for commercial supply and revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NSS revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is expected to be flat. FY28 growth should be similar to the core business, and the NSS target EBITDA margin is close to 30% after supply chain changes.

544626|2026-03.headline: Exato Technologies FY26 revenue rose about 35% to Rs 168 crore and PAT about 67% to Rs 16.09 crore, with management guiding 50-60% growth for FY27.
544626|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew about 35% to Rs 168 crore and PAT grew about 67% to Rs 16.09 crore, with PAT margin up from 7.77% to 9.58%. Q4 EBITDA margin fell, which management attributed to heavy investment in US and Australia hiring, travel, events and leadership additions. Management said the order book closed at about Rs 600 crore (up from about Rs 520 crore in December), and it is pivoting toward international markets, AI-as-a-service, ERP and an infrastructure (hardware) line. Q4 showed a sharp rise in purchase of software and hardware, which analysts questioned as margin-diluting.

segments.commentary: Management expects this to contribute 30-35% of revenue within 2-3 years and cited larger deals in pipeline; it was earlier a Cisco/HP business, now being rebuilt as a dedicated vertical.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI infrastructure deals and customers spending IT budgets in Q4 drove higher resale purchases; these are sold to customers, so they cannot be capitalised. Hardware margins are lower on transactional deals, and a dedicated infrastructure vertical with OEMs (HP, Cisco) is intended to improve margins.

qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 28-30% of FY26 revenue per management; target 50-55% in two years. Gross margin is 22-24% domestic and 30-35% international.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 380 crore unexecuted order book will bill in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30-35% of the Rs 380 crore will be billed in FY27, with the rest over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Target set at 3-4 years, supported by an inside sales team of about 20 people, a US senior hire from Tata Communications, and a planned event with about 2,500 customer database contacts.

544632|2026-06.headline: Meesho Q1 FY27: management says logistics cost per delivered order fell about ₹1 QoQ, and it guides to ~25% five-year NMV CAGR.

544632|2026-09.headline: Meesho Q2 FY27 contribution margin rose to about 6%, driven mainly by logistics efficiencies, with management reinvesting part of the gain into pricing.
544632|2026-09.overview: Management said the contribution margin improvement was led by logistics efficiencies (RTO reduction, higher order density, middle-mile network redesign, Valmo cost gains) rather than ad take-rate. Management cautioned the 6% CM should not be extrapolated, as part of the gain is held back for seller and consumer pricing once server costs normalise. Adjusted EBITDA margin was about minus 1% of NMV, with a quarterly FCF print helped by a roughly INR523 crore working capital release tied to festive-season timing shifting into September. Festive season sales were described as better than expectations, with traffic at all-time highs, though seller-side supply disruptions from crude and Middle East volatility were flagged.

qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh Bansal said Q2's 6% should not be extrapolated because of lead-lag in passing efficiencies to sellers and consumers. FY27 CM should be substantially better than FY26, and FY28 gains will come from ad monetisation rising as a share of NMV.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from ad take-rate versus logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics was the primary driver, covering RTO, density, network redesign and Valmo efficiency. Ad-rate details were not disclosed separately. There were no specific volume-slab pricing changes from 3PLs this quarter; these typically come in the December quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth not being used to keep CM high, and why pass pricing benefit back now?
qa_highlights.answer: Vidit Aatrey said pricing investments pay off over multiple quarters through the flywheel. Passing back CM would not add 10-15% growth immediately, but it makes more categories and sellers viable over the next 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any sign of rising CAC or churn given the ATU growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vidit said ATU growth partly reflects festive timing. Marketing is reallocated on CAC and LTV, with the same internal hurdle rates, and new-user growth in big cities is nearly as fast as in smaller towns.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fixed cost leverage not showing up, and what is the steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh said Q2 server costs were elevated by GPU capacity bought early for the festive season, with normalisation expected by Q4 FY27. Pre-festive marketing spend also front-loaded costs. Long-run fixed cost is targeted at about 3% of NMV.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working-capital release in Q2 reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh said the Q2 release reflects festive sales spilling into September. Normalised, a 20-day negative working capital cycle and 30% growth should yield about 1.5% of NMV positive FCF, and LTM FCF should turn positive in a few quarters.

544633|2026-03.headline: Vidya Wires FY26 revenue rose 24.2% to INR 18,396.4 mn and PAT reached INR 576.1 mn; ALCU plant began production on 7 Feb 2026.

544634|2026-03.headline: Aequs FY26 revenue rose 33% to INR12,304 million with a record Q4 of INR3,671 million; FY27 guides 45-50% consolidated growth and consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27.

Aerospace carried the year (revenue INR10,464 million, EBITDA margin about 27%), while consumer EBITDA loss widened to INR783 million. 544644|2026-03.headline: Corona Remedies Q4FY26 revenue rose 20.2% to INR 353 crore and FY26 PAT grew 33% (adjusted INR 199 crore), with Q4 EBITDA margin down ~90bps to 17.6%.

544644|2026-06.headline: Corona Remedies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with EBITDA margin up ~190 bps to 22%.

rows.why: Management says it is offsetting a possible 100 bps margin hit through other cost reductions to keep 20% PAT growth, and it is working to reduce employee cost from about 1,000 added MRs (35% of 3,111).

tone.note: Management was confident on India growth (22.7% vs IPM 11.6%), brand momentum and unchanged FY27 guidance, but cautious on margins and declined to extrapolate Q1 profitability; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, the Bayer-Zydus molecule's YoY decline and raw material inflation.

544644|2026-09.headline: Corona Remedies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR441 crores, with PAT up 15.3% to INR60 crores as D&A weighed.
544644|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 22.2% YoY to INR441 crores in Q2 FY27 and 22% in H1, with India business at 97% of revenue and 22.9% growth in Q2. EBITDA rose 22.3% to INR96 crores at a stable 21.7% margin, while PAT grew 15.3% to INR60 crores, held back by higher depreciation and amortisation from new facilities and acquired brands. Management reiterated guidance of 1.5x IPM growth (revenue about 15%) and PAT growth of about 20%, and said Wokadine integration and business-model change is running slower than expected. Infertility is the first new therapy push, with a 46-person task force reaching about INR7 lakh PCPM.

financial_highlights.change: +22.2% YoY vs INR361 crores in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Q2 INR12.6 crores; H1 INR25.3 crores

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Contributed 97% of revenue in Q2 and H1, growing 22.9% in Q2 vs about 12% for the Indian pharma market. Chronic portfolio grew about 29% vs 14.9% for the chronic market segment.

segments.name: Engine brands
segments.commentary: 33 engine brands contribute about 79-80% of India business and are growing about 22%. Management aims to build further brands to INR100 crores-plus.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Export revenue was INR12.6 crores in Q2 and INR25.3 crores in H1. Management expects about INR60-65 crores this year and about 15% growth next year; international to stay under 10% of revenue in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Wokadine (acquired from Bayer)
segments.commentary: Commercialised this year; base sales maintained in Q2, but integration and business-model change are slower than expected. Management still targets 25% CAGR over 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: Revenue guidance remains 1.5x IPM growth, which management equates to about 15% revenue growth assuming IPM at about 10%.
PAT guided to grow about 20%; no guidance given on operating margins, though margins are expected to improve in coming years after the 400+ MR addition.
IPM expected to grow low double digits (about 10-12%) over the next 3-4 quarters, per management's own view.
International revenue expected at INR60-65 crores this year, growing about 15% next year.
Hormone dossiers (10-12) to be filed over 2-3 years; registrations take 1-2 years after that.
No MR additions planned in CY27; possible addition of about 150 MRs in FY28.
capex_capacity: MR force at 3,111 medical representatives after about 400 added in Q4 FY26; no additions planned until FY28.

IVF task force of 46 people covers about 2,500 infertility professionals and gynaecologists (about 60 per rep), reaching about 75-80% of the market; PCPM about INR7 lakh in first 6 months, targeting INR8-9 lakh by year-end.
Newly commissioned facilities and acquired brands drove higher D&A in the quarter.
Hormone API backward integration via stake in La Chandra; forward integration through a plant in Ahmedabad.
demand_pricing: Indian pharma market grew about 12% in Q2 per PharmaTrac; September 2026 was the market's highest monthly growth at 13.5%, increasingly volume-led.
Over 3 years Corona grew 1.9x the market, with volume growth about 3.3x, new introductions about 2.2x and price about 1.2x the market.
Price growth in the 8.5-8.9% range in recent quarters vs about 5-5.5% historically; management cites NELM/non-NELM mix and market absorption.
Market share: about 0.77% of IPM; 2.3% in core therapies, which grow about 25% faster than IPM. Ranked 26th in the Indian pharma market; 14th among covered companies.
NLEM exposure about 7.5% of revenue (down from 9%); top-5 brand SKUs have 0% under NLEM. Management sees no impact yet from trade margin caps.
Semaglutide: Corona is in the top 10 semaglutide companies; management expects a INR1,200-1,400 crore molecule market in year one; focus stays on engine brands.
No change in competitive intensity observed from smaller branded players or alternate channels.

qa_highlights.question: How is the new therapy strategy (nephrology, CNS, rheumatology, derma) being executed, and is M&A considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Infertility is the first new therapy, with a task force formed in CY2026. Management is open to both organic and inorganic routes and is evaluating proposals, with nothing concrete yet.

qa_highlights.question: How has the Wokadine acquisition performed, and what is growth ex-Wokadine?
qa_highlights.answer: Base sales maintained in Q2 after full distribution and supply-chain integration. Business-model change is slower than expected; next two quarters give more visibility. Ex-Wokadine growth is 21.5% in Q2 and H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no operating-margin guidance. FY26 EBITDA margin was 20.9%, and margins are expected to improve in coming years after the 400+ MR addition.

qa_highlights.question: How is IVF scale-up progressing, and is the team being expanded?
qa_highlights.answer: The 46-person team reached about INR7 lakh PCPM in 6 months, with INR8-9 lakh targeted by year-end. No expansion in CY27; possible in H2 CY27 or early FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% revenue guidance be revised given stronger IPM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance remains 1.5x IPM. Management said upside exists if IPM stays at 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international business and hormones?
qa_highlights.answer: Preparing 10-12 hormone dossiers for regulated and semi-regulated markets, with 2-3 years to revenue. International is about 15% growth this year; less than 10% of revenue in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is price growth higher, and what is the plan for new therapy share?
qa_highlights.answer: Price growth is about 8.5-8.9% vs about 5-5.5% historically, driven by market absorption and NELM/non-NELM mix. Management expects new therapies to enter within 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the regulatory risk from price controls and trade margin caps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the pricing matter sub judice and declined detail. NLEM exposure is about 7.5% of revenue; trade margin caps are seen as a trade-channel issue with no impact so far.

risks_watch: Wokadine integration and business-model change are behind plan; the next two quarters will show whether the 25% CAGR target holds.
D&A from new facilities and acquired brands is compressing PAT growth (15.3%) below revenue growth (22.2%).

International growth was soft in H1; the 15% growth target depends on dossier filings and registrations.
IPM growth is strong now; management expects it to ease to low double digits, which would narrow the upside to the 1.5x guidance.
544644|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on core India growth and market outperformance, with specific figures. Noticeably cautious and hedged on Wokadine, international timelines, and IPM outlook (described as a "gut feel"), and evasive on margin guidance and valuation multiples.

The integration and change in business model are a little slower than expected.
So the estimation of 1.5x in the IPM has always been a guidance, and it will remain as the guidance as far as revenue is concerned.
So these 33 brands are potential INR 100 crores-plus brands, and we are working on it.

rows.label: Wokadine 25% CAGR target
rows.why: Base sales maintained in Q2 but business-model change is slower than expected; management still targets 25% CAGR over 3-4 years, and the next two quarters give more visibility.

rows.label: International INR60-65 crore FY27

rows.why: NLEM exposure is about 7.5% of revenue and management called the pricing matter sub judice; price growth of 8.5-8.9% vs 5-5.5% historically is a watch item.

544645|2026-03.headline: Park Medi World FY26 revenue rose 21% to INR1,679 crore and PAT 27% to INR274 crore, with gross debt cut to INR28 crore.
544645|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue INR1,679 crore (+21% YoY), EBITDA INR444 crore (+20%, 26% margin) and PAT INR274 crore (+27%, 16% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR460 crore (+30%), with operating EBITDA of INR127 crore (+44%, 28% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (+47%). The bed network grew 610 beds to 3,610 at March 2026 (3,960 including Panchkula, commissioned 10 April 2026), and management reiterated a target of 5,460 beds by March 2028. Gross debt fell to INR28 crore from INR450 crore, and debtor days fell to 129 from 161.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating EBITDA excl. other income (Q4 FY26)

financial_highlights.change: +7% YoY for FY; Q4 vs INR28,423 in Q4 FY25

segments.name: IPD
segments.commentary: FY26 IPD volume was 95,525 (+18% YoY, highest ever); Q4 FY26 IPD was 25,329 (+29% YoY per the call).

segments.name: OPD
segments.commentary: FY26 OPD volume was about 7.78 lakh (+22% YoY); Q4 FY26 was about 1.88 lakh (+13% YoY). Total patients served about 8.7 lakh in FY26.

segments.name: High-end specialties
segments.commentary: About 56.9% of revenue came from high-end specialties in FY26, up 316 bps YoY. Oncology was about 6.5% of FY26 revenue versus 5% in FY25, and about 8% in Q4 FY26 versus 6% in Q4 FY25.

guidance_outlook: Bed capacity: 850 beds to be added in FY27 (350 Panchkula already commissioned, 200 Narela targeted for Q2 FY27, 300 Kanpur) and about 1,000 in FY28 (400 Gorakhpur, 200 Ambala oncology extension, 150 Mohali, 250 Rohtak Greenfield, which management said comes January 2028). Target 5,460 beds by March 2028 and, between FY28 and FY33, nearly 10,000 beds.

Capex: about INR55 crore planned in FY27 and about INR250 crore in FY28; management cited about INR500 crore total over the next two years. Capex per bed is about INR34 lakh through the 5,460-bed plan.

CGHS rate hike of about 12-15% is expected to add about 7-7.5% to revenue for nine months of FY27. Management's net impact estimate is 5-6% of total revenue. Actual flow-through likely visible after Q1 FY27.
Payor mix is expected to move from about 80:20 (government insurance vs cash/TPA) toward 75:25 and then 70:30 over 12-18 months. Management's end-FY26 target was about 65-70% government insurance.

Agra (commissioned February 2026) is adding about INR5 crore revenue per month, expected to contribute about INR90 crore revenue in FY27 and turn EBITDA positive. Bathinda (250 beds) is running at 65-70% occupancy.
Debtor days are expected to fall below 100 eventually, but management said this will take time; near-term target around four months of government collection cycle.
capex_capacity: Bed network: 3,000 beds at start of FY26, 3,610 at 31 March 2026, 3,960 with Panchkula (350 beds, commissioned 10 April 2026, capex about INR125 crore). Target 5,460 by March 2028.

Two FY26 additions: Bathinda 250 beds (acquired, Punjab) and Agra 360 beds (UP entry, commissioned February 2026). Narela, Delhi (200 beds, IBC acquisition): total capex about INR80 crore, of which INR55 crore spent. Kanpur (300 beds): about INR30 crore to invest.

Greenfield break-even takes 12-15 months and full recovery 2.5-3 years, per management. Acquired assets' EBITDA break-even is about 3-3.5 years on a weighted average basis; acquisition investment recovered through revenue in roughly 11 months.
Liquidity: FDs of about INR314 crore, about INR100 crore in bank, and INR135 crore non-current FDs at 31 March 2026. Management expects only a small debt raise if any.
demand_pricing: Management says ARPOB is kept in the affordable range and is one of several profitability drivers; expenses should be benchmarked to revenue, not ARPOB alone.
Demand described as strong across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, with patients who previously travelled to metros now treated locally.

Collections are described as close to 100% by management. Government (central) accounts for 92% of debtors; government bills are cleared in about three months, and management is seeking to shorten this.
Disallowance on government revenue stayed at about 9% in Q4 FY26.
Oncology is being expanded across all 16 hospitals (medical and surgical), with radiation oncology in three hospitals.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin expansion, seasonality, CGHS or case mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mainly higher occupancy at existing hospitals; Agra began operations in February 2026 and Bathinda in May (per CFO), so new units did not drive Q4 margins.

qa_highlights.question: Provision for receivables at FY26 end?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the provision made at 31 March 2026 is close to INR200 crore under Ind AS.

qa_highlights.question: Cost and break-even profile of Greenfield and acquired hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Greenfield EBITDA break-even in 12-15 months, with recovery over 2.5-3 years. Brownfield units such as Bathinda were said to turn PAT-positive within the first month. Acquisitions were said to recover investment via revenue in about 11 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much CGHS benefit flows into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 7-7.5% uplift for nine months of FY27 and a net impact of 5-6% of revenue after mix, largely flowing to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone revenue down QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Bathinda was operated under O&M by Park Medi World until it became a subsidiary on 5 January 2026; consolidated revenue is unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex or debt constraining growth beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is not being curbed. Capex needs are funded internally, with debt possible for large acquisitions, and it targets about 10,000 beds between FY28 and FY33.

qa_highlights.question: Doctor attrition and incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consultant attrition is among the lowest, citing clinicians not being measured on volume. Bonuses go to clinicians above the 75th percentile on patient satisfaction and clinical outcomes.

risks_watch: Receivables: 92% of debtors are central government; collection timing and the roughly INR200 crore provision are key to working capital.
Payor mix shift toward government insurance and CGHS rates, with net impact of 5-6% of revenue, depends on implementation timing after Q1 FY27.
Execution of 1,500 beds by March 2028, including Narela (Q2 FY27) and Kanpur; Greenfield ramp-ups carry a 12-15 month loss-making period.
Cost inflation (doctor salaries, consumables) versus ARPOB growth of about 7%; management asked analysts to benchmark costs to revenue rather than ARPOB.
Oncology drug pricing under CGHS: management said it supplied cancer drugs at minimal profit under negotiated vendor rates.

544645|2026-06.headline: Park Medi World Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs.476 crore, PAT up 35% to Rs.89 crore; FY27 guided to Rs.2,080 crore revenue.
544645|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.476 crore (+19% YoY) with EBITDA excluding other income of Rs.126 crore (26.5% margin) and PAT of Rs.89 crore (18.6% margin, +220 bps). PAT growth was attributed mainly to lower interest outgo after term debt repayment. Occupancy fell to 56% from 68% as 960 new beds (Bhatinda, Agra, Panchkula) entered the denominator. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs.2,080 crore, EBITDA Rs.530 crore and PAT Rs.360 crore, and announced two acquisitions (Rudrapur, commissioned 2 August 2026; Zirakpur/Mehar, Rs.107 crore valuation).

vs 68% in Q1 FY26; FY26 was 64%

segments.commentary: Contributed about 62% of revenue, up 440 bps YoY from about 57%. Neurology about 14.5%, cardiology about 12%, urology about 11%, joint replacement about 9.5%, oncology 9-10%, gastroenterology about 7%.

segments.name: Newer hospitals (Agra, Panchkula, Bhatinda)
segments.commentary: Agra (commissioned Feb 2026) and Panchkula (commissioned Apr 2026) are ramping in line with plan; management expects no EBITDA loss, with first-year margins of about 10-12%. Mohali, the mature comparable, is at about 26% margin.

EBITDA margin expected at 26.7-27% for FY27; PAT margin 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook given bed additions, ARPOB and occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 revenue Rs.2,080 crore (+24%), EBITDA Rs.530 crore (+25%) and PAT Rs.360 crore (+32%); mature hospitals are growing 18-20%. ARPOB guided at 10-12%, with hospitals above 60% occupancy at 30-31% EBITDA and sub-60% at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Greenfield units (Panchkula, Agra) show EBITDA losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no EBITDA loss is expected; new units start at about 10-12% margin in year one versus 26% at Mohali, and blended margin stays at 26-27%.

qa_highlights.question: How will Rudrapur and Zirakpur ramp up, and what are their financials?
qa_highlights.answer: Rudrapur (330 beds, previously about Rs.55-56 crore revenue on 200 beds) targets Rs.100 crore revenue, EBITDA Rs.20-22 crore, PAT Rs.12-13 crore in year one, then Rs.140 crore, EBITDA Rs.35-36 crore, PAT Rs.21-22 crore. Zirakpur targets Rs.70-75 crore revenue at 25-26% EBITDA in its first year of operation, commissioning November 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Incremental capex at Agra and Rudrapur, and capex per bed given acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Agra needed Rs.7.5 crore of equipment and upgrades on top of the Rs.245 crore acquisition cost; Rudrapur needs Rs.10-12 crore additional. Management says blended capex per bed stays at about Rs.36 lakh on Rs.767 crore for 2,130 beds over FY27-FY28, including acquisitions, with Palam Vihar at about Rs.25 lakh per bed.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the CGHS rate revision on ARPOB and EBITDA, and whether oncology faces pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CGHS revision (12-15%, October 2025) gives about 7-7.5% net ARPOB benefit given 70% CGHS patients, with full impact from Q2-Q4; the benefit will be redeployed into equipment and maintenance so EBITDA impact is limited. It reported no CGHS pressure in oncology, which is 9-10% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 bed guidance now 4,740 versus the earlier expectation, and is promoter dilution planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap versus the earlier figure reflects 250 new beds (100 at Palam Vihar, 150 at Zirakpur) not in earlier communication; 1,000 beds in FY28 remain intact. On promoter stake, it said the minimum roughly 8% divestment is due by December 2028, with no timeline given and equity raise linked to an acquisition.

544657|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose 37.19% to INR256.92 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to about 11% in H2 on forex and RCN prices; management guides 15-16%.
544657|2026-03.overview: Pajson Agro's first earnings call after its December listing covered FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026). Total income grew 37.19% YoY to INR256.92 crore, EBITDA grew 24.98% and PAT grew 21.4%, with the company maintaining a double-digit full-year EBITDA margin. H2 saw margin compression from a spike in raw cashew nut (RCN) prices, forex movement (rupee moved about 10.5% from April 2025 base) and shipping disruptions, with H2 total income up 37.38% to INR138.5 crore and H2 PAT up 8.97%. Capacity utilisation was 86% on an 18,000 MT Andhra Pradesh plant, and a greenfield 35,000 MT Vizianagaram facility (targeting 70,000 MT total by FY30) is being built with INR39.53 crore of POs committed by March 2026.

544657|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 total income rose 23% YoY to about INR 145 crore, with EBITDA of about INR 20 crore (14% margin) and PAT of about INR 12.6 crore.
544657|2026-09.overview: Pajson Agro reported H1 FY27 total income of about INR 145 crore (up 23% YoY), EBITDA of about INR 20 crore at a 14% margin, and PAT of about INR 12.6 crore. Plant utilisation rose to about 95% from 86% in FY26, with management saying demand is now ahead of capacity. The board approved a share-swap acquisition of 100% of Pacific Global FZCO, which runs a 60,000 MT cashew processing facility in Cote d'Ivoire, while the 35,000 MT Vizianagaram plant has slipped about 45 days after cyclones and is now expected to start trials by February. Margin compression versus last year was attributed to forex, freight and sourcing cost pressure.

qa_highlights.answer: Realisation is about 15% lower per kg than India (current India H1 realisation about INR 170/kg RCN); Pulkit Jain said Africa margins are higher than India, with margin benefit from farm-gate sourcing expected in the long term rather than FY27-28.

qa_highlights.answer: Aayush Jain cited forex movement, freight and shipping surcharges that rose mid-season, and a stronger H1 FY26 base due to earlier festivities.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the change in market share, flows vs MTM?

544664|2026-03.headline: KSH International Q4 FY26 revenue rose 101% YoY to INR 1,018 crore and EBITDA per ton reached about INR 74,000, with FY26 PAT at a record INR 110 crore.

segments.commentary: Grew 58% in FY26 and 80% in Q4 YoY. Management is targeting EVs, AC compressors and motors. About 35% of the 43,445 MT installed capacity is standard.

544679|2026-03.headline: Amagi FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,506 crores and turned PAT positive at INR 72 crores, swinging about INR 140 crores from a FY25 loss.
544679|2026-03.overview: Amagi reported its first full year as a listed company, with FY26 revenue of INR 1,506 crores (up 30% reported, 23% constant currency) and Q4 revenue of INR 397 crores (up 29%). Adjusted EBITDA rose to about INR 156 crores (10% margin) from INR 23 crores, and PAT was INR 72 crores versus a loss of INR 69 crores in FY25. Management stressed net revenue retention of 126% and growth across all three segments, while flagging Q4 gross margin compression tied to customer pricing, AI costs and parallel-running of lower-cost alternatives. NEWSPULSE, the first agentic AI product, has its first paying customer and is in trials with news networks.

Gross margin: management said not to extrapolate quarterly moves to full year and expects volume growth to offset modest CPM/price compression; the gross margin impact of NEWSPULSE is too early to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: Sales headcount efficiency and how many accounts one salesperson can handle over 3 to 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Does accelerating monetized impression growth reflect market conditions, and how exposed is revenue to advertising macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Impression growth reflects the shift to streaming. Customers' ad economics flow through to Amagi pricing with a lag; no impact seen yet, though geopolitics is a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count trend and new customer additions, which have slowed on a quarterly basis.
qa_highlights.answer: Customer count rose to 492 in FY26 from 463 and 396 earlier; Q4 added 27 and churned 30, mainly year-end cleanup of sub-USD 1,000 accounts. Growth is coming from the existing base and upmarket enterprise deals.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and acquisition plans, and CC NRR.

544679|2026-06.headline: Amagi's July 7, 2026 "AI in Media" webinar was industry-level only; no quarterly financials, guidance or Amagi-specific metrics were disclosed.
544679|2026-06.overview: This transcript is of an educational investor webinar titled "AI in Media", hosted by Amagi on July 7, 2026 and filed under Regulation 30, not an earnings call. The moderator stated upfront that company financial performance, outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed. The CEO Baskar Subramanian framed AI as reshaping the video value chain across production, preparation (metadata, encoding, scheduling), distribution (agent-to-agent deals) and consumer discovery. He cited a claim that every $1 spent on technology brings $2 to $4 of human toil, and said most customers view AI as expansionary rather than a cost-saving tool today. No Q1 FY27 results, segment data or guidance were given.
guidance_outlook: No company guidance given; the moderator stated financial performance, business outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed.
Management described AI-driven production cost deflation as a multi-year shift, saying the next few years would bring a fundamental change, without quantifying it.
Management said outcome-based pricing is early and not yet visible in media, and that the core system is expected to stay as is while expansion revenue is driven by outcomes.
capex_capacity: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPUs and servers, and expects more progression in that direction; no Amagi capex or capacity figures were given.
Management said GPU costs are significant for video AI but did not quantify them; token cost is a small part of AI cost in video.
demand_pricing: Management says most customers are pursuing expansion (more channels, revenue opportunities) rather than AI cost savings today, citing Jevons' paradox.
Outcome-based pricing (per transaction, per result, per success) is being discussed in some markets, but management says it is not yet visible in media.

Management says token cost is a small part of AI cost in video; GPU costs are significant. It also cited an example of a scheduler's work falling from 8 hours to about 10 minutes of review under an agentic system.
Management described the metadata and preparation workload as a headcount constraint, with media companies creating about 6 hours of unique news daily and running content across 40-plus countries.

qa_highlights.question: What safeguards exist against hallucination and unpredictability given strict 99.9999% SLAs with clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the approach is to bring determinism to a non-deterministic problem through guardrails and engineered systems, noting that getting AI from demos to production is the hard part.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI improving prep-work speed and reducing pricing through deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI mainly reduces human cost in preparation (e.g., speech-to-text making subtitling unnecessary) and expands what can be done rather than directly reducing price.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI move production and pre-production workflows to the cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPU and server capacity, and expects more of this shift.

qa_highlights.question: Are there real-life examples of cost reduction or higher OTT/cable content from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is early, with some creators using AI for VFX and background creation, and microdrama as the most active area.

qa_highlights.question: Is there evidence of cost savings, given higher token costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token cost is small relative to video GPU and human costs, and most customers are using AI for expansion, with cost savings secondary.

qa_highlights.question: Do agent-to-agent communications create network effects and first-mover advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said connecting two or more ecosystem parties through agentic infrastructure has high network-effect value, but the space is very early and standards are still forming.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI deepen client engagement and threaten horizontal SaaS or hyperscalers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that vertical, mission-critical media software has a moat in enterprise context, which it sees as more durable than generic reasoning models.

qa_highlights.question: Will agentic AI materially cut customer operating costs and create pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-job costs may deflate, but the volume of work customers want to do is expanding, which it characterised as a Jevons' paradox effect.

qa_highlights.question: How will vendor-client commercial models change as agentic AI spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outcome-driven pricing is being explored in other industries, but it is early and not yet prominent in media.

risks_watch: Hallucination and unpredictability of agentic AI against strict uptime SLAs, which management said it addresses with guardrails but gave no metrics for.
Rising GPU and infrastructure costs for video AI, which management said are material but did not quantify.
Possible shift in vendor pricing toward outcome-based models, which would change revenue recognition, though management said it is not yet visible.
The webinar did not address Amagi's own Q1 FY27 numbers, so the company's operating and financial trajectory remains unassessed; the company directed investors to ir@amagi.com for follow-up.

544681|2026-03.headline: INDO SMC guided FY27 revenue to INR450-500 crores on an INR237 crore order book plus INR125 crore fresh orders, with margins targeted at 15%+.
544681|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year after listing, with management saying revenue roughly doubled and PAT more than doubled, driven by higher-value CT/PT, bus duct, meter cubicle and panel products. Management attributed a softer March-quarter SMC and FRP output to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum-product price swings and supply gaps. The company shifted to shorter (2-3 month) orders with price-escalation clauses (5% trigger) and said it is now choosing orders on margin. Inventory rose to about INR85 crores (around 100 days) because of pre-stocked raw materials, and the working capital cycle was cut from 83 to about 40 days. Management did not give a precise FY26 revenue or margin figure in the call; the 15% EBITDA margin cited by analysts was not confirmed by management.

rows.label: Rajasthan expansion beyond Gujarat
rows.why: Management noted Rajasthan expansion with early market response, but no revenue or capacity figures were given.

rows.label: Order book conversion in FY27
rows.why: Management cited 20-80% conversion of the order book in FY27, but the transcript is unclear and the range is too wide to rely on.

rows.label: Receivables and payables both elevated (~106 days)
rows.why: Management said the rise is project-specific to the 65 MW project and that receivables and payables are matched, so net impact is limited, but collection on that project is a watch item.

tone.note: Management was confident on the RESCO/O&M model and EPC growth but cautious on margins, acknowledging dilution from the low-margin back-to-back project, and declined FY28/FY29 capacity targets; analysts pushed on margins, capacity, order book conversion and working capital.

544684|2026-03.headline: Digilogic FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR78.27 crore and PAT 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, but a ~INR22 crore spillover from delayed imported hardware missed the 20-25% growth guidance.
544684|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income rose 8.4% YoY to INR78.27 crore, with EBITDA up 16.5% to INR15.18 crore and margin expanding 152 bps to 19.6%. PAT grew 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR12.63 crore. Management attributed the shortfall versus its January 2026 growth guidance to delayed imported OEM hardware, which pushed about INR22 crore of orders into FY27. Management guided to 20-25% growth for FY27, contingent on converting INR100-plus crore of orders by September 2026, and announced new subsidiary Abhedhya (RF systems), an SBC R&D effort, and Project UDAN manufacturing expansion.

segments.name: Measurement equipment
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue; management said most of its value comes from software content with little material cost, supporting the margin gain.

segments.name: Checkout systems
segments.commentary: About 22% of FY26 revenue; ATEs about 17%. Management said ATE and checkout value was broadly flat YoY, and the share fell because measurement equipment grew.

segments.name: Prototyping vs production
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 30% of revenue from prototyping and 70% from production orders. This was not reconciled with a reported figure and was described as approximate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25%, reiterated on the call; management said it is confident of meeting it.
Management targets INR100-plus crore of purchase orders by end-September 2026, with billing for FY27 expected to be supported by that order intake.
Order book was about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026, with most expected to bill by August 2026.

Project UDAN (new manufacturing facility, about four times the current capacity) expected operational by mid-2028; indicative revenue INR11-13 crore in FY29, INR28-30 crore in FY30, INR57-61 crore in FY31.
Current setup capacity estimated at INR150-160 crore revenue potential.
Abhedhya (RF subsidiary) expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months; management indicated revenue in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Project UDAN: a manufacturing and environmental testing facility, about four times current size; mid-2028 target; can deliver 20-25 systems per six months versus about six currently.
Guest house under construction; capitalised finance cost on exposure of about INR2.1 crore (not fully drawn), borrowing at REPO plus 2.5%.
Abhedhya, a new RF subsidiary for radar, EW and communication subsystems, with a 1-year build-and-demonstrate timeline.
R&D: custom single board computer (SBC) built in-house by an eight-member team, about 1.5-2 years old; qualification range -20 to +85 degrees C; environmental testing not yet completed.
Management said two to three new R&D products are in development.
demand_pricing: FY26 execution was held back by imported hardware from US/European OEMs; lead time rose from about 2 months to about 4 months, leaving roughly INR22 crore spilled into April 2026. Management said about INR20 crore additional revenue would otherwise have closed in FY26.

Order book fell to about INR31 crore from INR46 crore; the tender pipeline fell to about INR110 crore from INR200 crore. Management attributed this to Government fund reallocation and said projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than lost.
Management said OEMs are rerouting shipments, adding a week or 10 days and roughly 1-2% cost.
Competitors named: Data Patterns and Zen Technologies, mainly in prototyping. Management said production work under DCPP is nomination-based with limited competition.
Customer base is 100% government in substance (DRDO, BDL, BEL, public sector defence production agencies), with some transactions billed through BDL.
Management said the export route is via DRDO and BDL systems, and MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at the evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 guidance of 20-25% growth missed, and what supports FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported hardware arrived about 4 months after order rather than 2, leaving roughly INR22 crore of spillover. Management cited INR30-plus crore of orders in hand by 30 May and a target of INR100-plus crore of POs by September.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from INR46 crore to INR31 crore and the pipeline from INR200 crore to INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government fund reallocation changed priorities and projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than cancelled. The INR100-plus crore target covers only projects with budgets allocated or tenders out.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue comes from production versus prototyping?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 30% prototyping and 70% production, and deferred exact figures to the CFO. No reported split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up Abhedhya as a separate company rather than a division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RF work needs different people, salaries, infrastructure and design expertise than TMS, and separate accountability is needed. Tender qualification is to be built by demonstrating products first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ATE and checkout share fall from about 44% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said measurement equipment, mostly software value add with low material cost, grew to a similar scale, and ATE and checkout value was broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the order book converting to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current orders should bill by about August 2026. Pipeline orders are expected as POs by end-September, with 2-3 months of build and about one month of installation, and cash collection around Aug-Oct.

risks_watch: Import dependence: US and European OEM hardware lead times stretched to about 4 months, and a repeat would repeat the FY26 spillover.
Order book of INR31 crore against FY27 growth target; the INR100-plus crore PO target by September 2026 is the key checkpoint.
Tender pipeline down from INR200 crore to INR110 crore; delays of 6-8 months attributed to Government budget reallocation.
Revenue mix is a management estimate (30% prototyping, 70% production), not a reported figure.
Project UDAN and Abhedhya are not yet operational; Abhedhya revenue is expected only in FY28, and the SBC still needs environmental qualification.
Governance: management's FY26 growth guidance was missed, and the call shows the company's first results call as a newly listed SME.
544684|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 targets and on the causes of the FY26 miss, which management attributes to imported-hardware delays. Less specific on the revenue split, timelines for UDAN and Abhedhya, and the exact reasons for the pipeline fall. Several answers were deferred to the CFO or to a future call.
key_quotes: So, my target is by September, by September I should have purchase orders in hand close to INR100-plus crores, with which our billing will be comfortably meeting the targets which have been projected.

Imagine a scenario, everything would have gone in the right direction without this international disturbances had these items come on time, I would have comfortably closed additionally INR20 crores apart from INR76 crores what we have closed.
Only thing is that might get delayed by few months, maybe 6 to 8 months, which might spill over to subsequent financial year. But opportunities are not lost.

financial_highlights.change: Turned positive; prior year not stated

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 152 bps to 19.6% in FY26 on software-heavy measurement equipment (49% of revenue, little material cost), but OEM rerouting adds 1-2% cost and FY27 margin guidance was not given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Project UDAN (about 4x current size, 20-25 systems per six months vs about six now) is targeted for mid-2028, so it adds no FY27 capacity; current setup capacity is INR150-160 crore revenue potential against FY26 revenue of INR78.27 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27, billing by August 2026 and POs by end-September
rows.why: FY27 growth guided at 20-25% (one transcript quote says 25-30%, a source conflict), backed by INR30-plus crore order book as of 30 May 2026 and a target of INR100-plus crore of POs by September 2026, against FY26 growth of 8.4%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Project UDAN and guest house are already committed, but no new capex has been announced beyond them and utilisation was not disclosed, so further capex depends on order conversion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 growth of 8.4% missed the 20-25% guidance, and the order book fell to INR31 crore from INR46 crore, so there is no basis for an upgrade yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The FY27 target depends on converting INR100-plus crore of POs by September 2026 from an INR30-plus crore order book, and the tender pipeline fell to INR110 crore from INR200 crore with 6-8 month delays; FY26 already missed guidance by spilling about INR22 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Abhedhya demo in 8-12 months; revenue in FY28
rows.why: Abhedhya RF subsidiary expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months with revenue in FY28 not FY27, the SBC still lacks environmental testing, and management says 2-3 new R&D products are in development.

rows.label: Order conversion to billing by Aug 2026
rows.why: Order book of about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026 with most expected to bill by August 2026, the first test of FY27 growth.

rows.label: Export via Sperry and Eirad MoUs
rows.why: MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains, with no revenue figure given.

rows.label: Receivables and collections
rows.why: Receivables are INR42.87 crore with INR2.31 crore older than 180 days, and pipeline cash collection is expected around Aug-Oct, against a working capital cycle of 3.46 times up from 1.6 times.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 targets and on blaming the FY26 miss on imported-hardware delays, but was vague on the revenue split, UDAN and Abhedhya timelines, and the pipeline fall; analysts pushed on the order book drop and the guidance miss.

544684|2026-09.headline: Digilogic H1 FY27 revenue rose 91% to INR34.96 crores and PAT rose 151% to INR4.76 crores, with management reiterating 25-30% FY27 top-line growth.
544684|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue grew 91% to INR34.96 crores from INR18 crores, EBITDA rose 126% to INR7.81 crores, and PAT grew 151% to INR4.76 crores. Management said H2 is seasonally much stronger in defense, citing FY26 revenue of INR78 crores split as H1 INR19 crores and H2 INR59 crores. Order book of INR20 crores is to be billed by mid-February 2027, with a further INR54 crores in pipeline at various tender stages. Management also reiterated 25-30% top-line and 30-35% EBITDA/PAT growth guidance for FY27, though analysts noted that the EBITDA guidance was lowered from 45-50% and that H1 margin gains were partly driven by FD interest income.

financial_highlights.value: INR78 crores (H1 INR19 crores, H2 INR59 crores)

segments.name: Test, measurement and simulation systems (TMS)
segments.commentary: Core business, described as the heart of operations; 36 projects executed in H1 FY27 valued at around INR33.18 crores. Customers include PSUs and DRDO agencies. Management expects TMS to keep growing at 20-30% a year.

segments.name: Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary, R&D)
segments.commentary: New experts hired for R&D; commercial production expected in H2 FY29 if plans hold. Management did not disclose financials.

segments.name: Project Udaan (new facility, build-to-print and build-to-spec)
segments.commentary: Civil construction is ongoing, with first-floor roof concrete complete; completion targeted by March 2027 and operations by end-2027. Management expects certification around Q1 2028 and commercialisation in about two years, with contribution starting FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guidance of 25-30%, which management said it expects to meet; CFO said the company expects to touch its guidance number.
EBITDA and PAT growth guidance of 30-35%. The CFO said the 40-45% figure in the earlier outlook included FD interest income, and core growth stays at 30-35%.
Management said the current margins are sustainable, with no guidance to expand or contract.
Order book of INR20 crores and pipeline of INR54 crores targeted for billing by mid-February 2027.
Project Udaan: civil construction completion by March 2027, internal testing by December 2027, inspection and certification in Q1 2028, and about three months to get the certificate.
High Precision GIMBAL System and custom single-board computer products expected to be marketable around mid-2027, adding an estimated INR3-4 crores a year initially, with break-even thereafter.
Ongoing internal SOP and technology upgrade expected to finish between December 2026 and March 2027.
capex_capacity: Project Udaan is a new facility whose civil construction is in progress. Management expects operations from end-2027 and certification around Q1 2028.
Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary) is expected to start commercial production in H2 FY29.
Management said the Udaan facility will cover both build-to-spec (in-house design) and build-to-print (production of designs supplied by clients), with build-to-print expected to contribute first.
Inventory rose in H1 because of work-in-progress and pre-ordered long-lead items for orders due by mid-February 2027. Management said this stock will be consumed by March.
demand_pricing: Management said the order book is INR20 crores and the pipeline INR54 crores, with about 60% of the pipeline being repeat orders. Total of around INR74 crores is described as converted from the INR110 crores tender pipeline cited in May 2026.
All INR22 crores of order spillover from the prior period was billed in H1 FY27, according to management.
Management said it could not share the split of the INR54 crores between technical evaluation, commercial negotiation and pending purchase orders. Government procurement timelines vary.
Competitive moat: management said customised boards, signal processing and software go through R&QA certification by government agencies, which it says takes 2-3 years to replicate.
Analysts asked for a segment split. The CFO said the H1 segment data was not readily available and would be shared later.
The company said it has no export sales; all revenue is domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EBITDA guidance reduced from 45-50% to 30-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said core growth is 30-35%; the earlier 40-45% figure included FD interest income. He said the core growth guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Was the INR22 crore spillover from the last call completed in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said all spillover orders were billed in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H1 margin improvement driven by, including software value-add?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the margin gains are driven by FD interest income, with fixed costs steady. He said the gains are across the board and not from software or revenue mix, and that segment-level analysis had not been done for the limited review.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 revenue reach the guidance (INR100 crore-plus implied H2 of about INR65 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said the 25-30% target is supported by the INR20 crore order book and the INR54 crore pipeline; he called anything above it a bonus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and role of the new Udaan facility, and what does it add to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said Udaan will start contributing in FY28 and that TMS will continue to grow alongside it. Management declined to quantify the Udaan revenue contribution.

qa_highlights.question: How do defense program delays (QRSAM, P-75I, NGC) affect the order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said Digilogic is part of about 10 programmes, of which 3-4 have moved into production, so TMS has not been impacted by the delays.

risks_watch: Order book is INR20 crores, lower than earlier disclosures; the INR54 crore pipeline is not yet awarded and management would not give a split by stage.
H2 must deliver about INR65 crores of revenue to reach FY27 guidance (implied by analyst math), which is heavily dependent on billing by mid-February 2027.
Project Udaan has schedule risk: civil completion by March 2027, certification in Q1 2028, then about 3 months for certification. Management did not quantify Udaan revenue.
Margin gains partly came from FD interest income; the company has not yet split segment profitability.
Government procurement delays; sales cycles depend on tender stages and purchase orders.
Segment revenue split and export data were requested but not provided on the call; the company said it would follow up.
544684|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the 25-30% top-line and 30-35% profit guidance, but evasive on order-conversion specifics, the INR54 crore pipeline stage split, Udaan revenue, and segment data. Management often repeated the same figures and said further detail would come later.
key_quotes: We are confident of achieving a growth of 25% to 30% top line, 30% to 35% in EBITDA and PAT.
Typically in defense industry, H2 is a much stronger period compared to H1.
So, the current margins that we have delivered, we are confident of sustaining it going forward.
Anything more than that is going to be a bonus.

rows.why: Management said current margins are sustainable with no guidance to expand; H1 gains were partly FD interest income and EBITDA guidance was cut to 30-35% from 45-50%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY28 (Udaan operations end-2027, certification Q1 2028)
rows.why: Project Udaan civil construction is ongoing with completion targeted March 2027 and operations by end-2027, but Udaan revenue is not quantified and contribution starts FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue up 91% to INR34.96 crores in H1; FY27 guided at 25-30% growth on INR78 crores FY26 base, backed by INR20 crore order book and INR54 crore pipeline (about 60% repeat orders).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex for Udaan is already under way; no utilisation figure was disclosed and no new capex was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: MD called anything above 25-30% a bonus and the order book is only INR20 crores, lower than earlier disclosures, so upside is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must deliver about INR65 crores against INR34.96 crores H1 revenue; FY26 H2 was INR59 crores vs H1 INR19 crores, and the INR20 crore order book plus INR54 crore pipeline (not split by stage) must bill by mid-Feb 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: High Precision GIMBAL System and custom single-board computer products expected marketable around mid-2027, adding an estimated INR3-4 crores a year initially.

rows.label: Project Udaan certification and commercialisation
rows.why: Civil completion targeted March 2027, internal testing December 2027, certification Q1 2028 with about three months to get the certificate; revenue not quantified by management.

rows.label: INR20 crore order book and INR54 crore pipeline billing by mid-Feb 2027
rows.why: INR20 crore order book is to be billed by mid-February 2027 and INR54 crore pipeline is at various tender stages with about 60% repeat orders, though the stage split was not disclosed.

rows.label: Internal SOP and technology upgrade
rows.why: Ongoing internal SOP and technology upgrade expected to finish in this window; no cost or margin figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 25-30% top-line and 30-35% profit guidance and on TMS growth of 20-30% a year, but evasive on order-conversion stages, Udaan revenue and segment data; analysts pushed on the EBITDA guidance cut from 45-50% and on FD interest income driving H1 margins.

544685|2026-03.headline: Shadowfax Q4 FY26 revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY) with record 4.5% PAT margin; FY26 PAT INR 112 crores.
544685|2026-03.overview: Management reported record Q4 FY26 growth and profitability: revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY, +6.7% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA about INR 58 crores (4.7% margin vs 4.3% in Q3 and 0.7% a year ago) and PAT INR 56 crores (4.5% margin). For FY26, revenue exceeded INR 4,200 crores (+69%), adjusted EBITDA was about INR 159 crores (roughly 3x FY25) and PAT was INR 112 crores vs INR 6 crores. Management guided to 27-30% overall growth, 100-120 bps adjusted EBITDA margin improvement through FY28, and FY27 capex of INR 180-190 crores, while investing in real estate, dark stores and large-shipment coverage.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.3% in Q3 FY26 and 0.7% in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Express parcel
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue; management says it is gaining share via new client wins, deeper engagement and value-added services such as same-day, next-day and reverse logistics. Top 2-3 customer concentration unchanged QoQ.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Grew more than 50% YoY and 16% QoQ in Q4; quick commerce volumes picked up and operations with Amazon Now commenced. Management guides 45-50% growth for this segment in the next year.

segments.name: Other logistics services
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 80 crores of the INR 1,200-plus crores quarterly revenue; wind-down of experimental services is largely complete as of Q4 FY26, with reshaping towards critical logistics.

guidance_outlook: Overall business growth guidance maintained at 27-30%; hyperlocal expected at 45-50% YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 100-120 bps over the next couple of years through FY28; 200-250 bps per year after FY28 until steady-state EBITDA.
Steady-state adjusted EBITDA margin viewed as sustainable at early double digits.
FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crores, flat in absolute terms vs FY26; dark stores to be less than 10% of capex.
Pin code coverage to rise from 15,600 (of 19,300) to about 17,000 by end FY27 and full country coverage by FY28; large-shipment pin codes from about 6,000 to 10,000 in FY27.
Plans to set up about 100 dark stores in FY27 for vertical quick commerce (about 15 today).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crores, flat in absolute terms vs FY26; dark stores less than 10% of capex.
Real estate footprint up 35% between September 2025 and March 2026 (leased last-mile and middle-mile sortation centres).
Touch points rose from 4,200 to 4,700 in about six months; opening about 120-150 pin codes per month.
OneNCR, one of the largest sorting centres, went live a few months back after about six months of dual costs; new last-mile hubs take six to eight months to reach efficiency.
Over the last three years more than 60% of capex went to sorting centres and about 85% to sorting centres plus last-mile hubs; strategy is to run a dual manual/automated setup.
demand_pricing: 3PL market share estimated at about 28-29% for Q4, up from about 17-18% a year earlier; growth split roughly 50-55% market growth and 40-45% share gains.
D2C and SME grew about 2.5x between FY25 and FY26; pricing 15-20% higher than enterprise customers; sales team expanded by more than 100 people.
Large-shipment business grew 3-4x vs FY25; currently serving about 6,000 pin codes.
Quick commerce: management says it maintains pricing as largest 3PL in the segment; works with six to seven QC platforms.
Lost shipments and QC debits about 6.1% of revenue in Q4 (6.3% in Q3, 5.7% in FY25); long-term target 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Where is market share gain coming from, and will it stabilise by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gains come from inefficient traditional 3PLs and some captive insourcing reversing; the top two players are gaining share and the market is consolidating. It did not give a stabilisation date.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY26 margin expansion look better as capex normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant operating leverage is yet to come, with opex from investments returning in FY27-FY28, and that H2 capex was made in advance for FY27 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Dark store unit economics and ROIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Top dark stores run at about 20%+ gross margin; breakeven in three to four months; average revenue INR 8-15 lakh per store per month; ROIC too early to quantify with 15 pilot stores.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance basis and service EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is on adjusted EBITDA only; management does not track service EBITDA. Part of the improvement comes from corporate operating leverage, with the rest from service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Lost shipment cost and white goods impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About half of the roughly 6% is quality-check debits from reverse logistics and half pure losses; management cited image-recognition upgrades and fixes in large-parcel damages in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Amazon Shipping and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive arms deprioritise external customers at peak, so they do not see such models working in India; D2C/SME is a meaningful double-digit share of revenue, not disclosed exactly.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and crude price volatility; fuel is under 10% of costs and contracts carry fuel surcharges, but customer demand for logistics could slow if fuel rises sharply.
Lost shipments and QC debits at about 6.1% of revenue, well above the 4-5% long-term goal; white goods expansion could add to losses.
Dual-cost drag from new sorting centres and last-mile hubs (six to eight months ramp) could weigh on near-term margins.
Hyperlocal YoY growth slowed in Q4 due to a strong prior-year Q4 base; competition in quick commerce crowdsourcing from platforms like LoadShare.
Dark store ROIC not yet proven at scale; 100-store target in FY27 is a new vertical.
Lower average shipment volume (volumetric weight) reduced realisation QoQ, per analyst question on yield dip.
544685|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, margins and the long-term network model, with strong claims on share gains and AI. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to split D2C revenue, dark-store ROIC, service EBITDA and client-level profitability, and kept guidance deliberately limited to adjusted EBITDA.
key_quotes: We believe in a business like this, early double -digit steady -state EBITDA margins are sustainable.
Our long-term goal was to bring it down to about 4% to 5%.
We don't talk about service EBITDA. We don't look at service EBITDA. We only look at adjusted EBITDA and that's what we are guiding everyone for.
Whatever we are growing today, whatever we are forecasting, I think 50%, 55% we are attributing to the underlying growth in 3PL market.

tone.note: Management was confident on share gains, pin code expansion, operating leverage and margin path, but cautious and evasive on D2C revenue split, dark store ROIC, service EBITDA and client profitability; analysts pushed on yield dip from volumetric weight, lost shipments and market share durability.

544685|2026-06.headline: Shadowfax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore; management raised FY27 growth guidance to 38-40% from 27-30%.
544685|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore and 10% QoQ, the fifth straight quarter of 65%+ growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose to INR67 crore (4.9% margin vs 4.7% in Q4) and PAT hit a record INR65 crore. Management attributed margin gains to lower lost-shipment costs (5.5% of revenue vs 6.1% in Q4) and efficiency work that absorbed diesel and labour cost pressure. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 38-40% while keeping the margin trajectory unchanged.

financial_highlights.change: vs 6.1% in Q4 and 7.9% a year ago
front-loaded ahead of peak season; 77% in network and automation
vs 27-29% last quarter (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Express Parcel
segments.commentary: Management cites share gains from consolidation between two large 3PL networks; pin codes at ~16,372 after adding ~716 in last 90 days. Prime (same/next-day D2C) grew 2.7x YoY with 400+ D2C customers; SF 360 self-serve has 1,200+ transacting sellers after ~90 days.

segments.name: Prime Large (LCV heavy deliveries)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR75 crore ARR, up close to 170% YoY and 25% QoQ. Reached 10,000 pin codes (FY27 target) in Q1; FY27 target raised to 12,000.

segments.name: Hyperlocal / Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Hyperlocal grew ~53% YoY and 17% QoQ. Amazon Now is a new customer with higher wallet share; Amazon has entered the top-10 customer club.

segments.name: Other logistics services (incl. CriticaLog and dark stores)
segments.commentary: Returned to sequential growth post CriticaLog integration. 47 of 100 planned dark stores live as of 30 June, with 20 more due; dark stores contribute ~10-12% of other logistics services revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 38-40% from earlier 27-30%; management cites enterprise visibility and new customers.
EBITDA margin trajectory unchanged; management says it will hold the margin guidance given at the start of the year (100-200 bps expansion path per analyst).
Dark store target of 100 for FY27; 47 live as of 30 June.
Prime Large pin code target raised to 12,000 for FY27 from 10,000 (already reached).
Lost shipment cost long-run target 3.5-4% of revenue, from 4.5-5% historically.
Minimum wage hikes in four states add roughly INR2-2.5 crore per month to costs.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of about INR60 crore, front-loaded before peak season; 77% went to network and automation (sortation centres, machines, IT, electrical).
Added more physical capacity and more pin codes in Q1 than any prior quarter; new pin codes run below capacity initially.
Dark stores live in six metro cities; store sizes range from 200-300 sq ft to 3,000-4,000 sq ft.
No dedicated infrastructure per service line; Prime and Prime Large run on shared hubs and trucks via segmented supply chain software.
demand_pricing: Management says consumption held up better than expected despite diesel price spike, gas supply issues and state elections.
Express market consolidation between two large 3PL networks is shifting volume to Shadowfax; marketplaces expanding into low-value (INR250 order) categories.
Quick commerce outsourcing: management claims 50%+ share of quick commerce outsourcing; industry outsourcing levels 12-15%, with capacity to reach 20-25%.
Express realisation around INR50 per shipment; management says weight, distance and service mix drive it more than Shadowfax controls.
Diesel: contracts allow pass-through, but Shadowfax lagged the increase by 5 days and absorbed the cost.

qa_highlights.question: What supports the raised growth guidance from Q2 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Bansal cited enterprise customer forward projections and visibility, plus new D2C and quick commerce customers (Amazon Now); he said the company is fairly confident in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 capex is for the growth upgrade versus beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is front-loaded before the peak season and the product mix is unchanged, with 77% in network and automation; the assets last 5+ years.

qa_highlights.question: Can the margin bridge be explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Praveen Kumar KJ said transport cost rose 0.1 pp to 18.8%, consumables rose 0.1 pp, and other costs rose 0.1 pp; lost-shipment cost fell 0.6 pp to 5.5%. Efficiency work offset larger cost increases; management says most of the cost impact is already in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the minimum wage hike?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2-2.5 crore per month across four states; management said much of the delta does not hit P&L because many staff earn incentives above minimum wage.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 dark store contribution disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined store-wise revenue but said all stores together contribute 10-12% of other logistics services revenue; it will provide more detail as the vertical matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is there cannibalisation between vertical dark-store quick commerce and SDD for D2C?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Bansal said SKU width differs (about 1 million SKUs for same-day vs up to 10,000 for dark-store delivery), so the models serve different needs in the same cities.

risks_watch: Diesel and crude-linked cost pressure; management absorbed a 5-day diesel pass-through lag.
Labour supply squeeze and minimum wage increases (INR2-2.5 crore per month).
Pricing pressure from listed anchor customers, which management says is managed through rate cards with volume-linked discounts.
Dependence on two large Express 3PL networks and on Amazon Now ramp-up.
Dark store economics still unproven at store level; 47 live of 100 target by year-end.
Upside growth guidance depends on new customer acquisition and sales-season volumes.
