544685|2026-09.headline: Shadowfax Q2 FY27 revenue rose 57% YoY to INR1,538 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin of 5%, its first time crossing INR1,500 crore and 5%.
544685|2026-09.overview: Revenue reached INR1,538 crore, up 57% YoY and 13% QoQ, despite no festive sales-season revenue in the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was INR77 crore at a 5% margin and PAT was INR67 crore. Operating space expanded from 53 lakh to 69 lakh sq ft ahead of the festive peak, and the delivery partner base grew 31% QoQ. Management kept the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance but declined to revise near-term guidance until Q3 performance is seen. Management also announced a micro-fulfillment centre (MFC) business and disclosed that exposure to the largest customer fell by at least 3-4 percentage points versus its long-term average.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR60 (from around INR55 last quarter)

segments.name: Express Parcel
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,096 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) on 21.7 crore shipments; share of revenue fell to 71% from 73% in Q1. Express realization was broadly flat QoQ and marginally down YoY.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Revenue INR341 crore (+88% YoY, +26% QoQ); share of revenue rose to 22% from 20%. Realization per order rose about 13% QoQ, helped by longer-distance food delivery after aggregators moved to 0% commission.

segments.name: Other logistics services (CriticaLog, Dark Stores, value-added)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR100 crore, up 13% QoQ, as CriticaLog (serving more than 550 customers) and Dark Stores scale. Value-added services are guided at 35%-40% of revenue.

segments.name: Prime Large (bulky)
segments.commentary: Annualized run rate above INR100 crore, up 33% QoQ; white goods and value-added services are in pilot.

segments.name: D2C and SME (Shadowfax 360)
segments.commentary: D2C business more than doubled YoY, with market share above 14% (up 2 pp QoQ). Shadowfax 360 has more than 6,700 sellers ordering within 200 days of launch.

guidance_outlook: Long-term cumulative revenue growth guidance of 27%-30% maintained; near-term guidance not revised until Q3 results are seen.
Express Parcel expected to grow at a 27%-28% CAGR, driven by market growth and share gains.
Quick commerce industry expected to compound at 30%+; Shadowfax assumes it keeps its market-leader share.
Capex guided at 3.8%-4% of revenue for the year, including MFC and Dark Store capex; management said the capex cycle is on track.
Micro-fulfillment centre business to be built over the next 6-12 months; revenue this year expected to be small.
Two mega sorters and volume profilers to go live in Q4 FY27; next lost-shipment feedstock target of 4% expected in a few quarters.
capex_capacity: Total operating space expanded from 53 lakh sq ft to 69 lakh sq ft in Q2, the largest capacity addition in company history.
Middle-mile footprint rose from 24 lakh sq ft to more than 34 lakh sq ft; about 5% of total space is temporary peak-season pop-ups that will wind down.
Dark Stores: 70 opened by end-Q2 FY27 against a target of 100 for the year, across 9 cities; more than 4,000 unique Dark Stores served across quick commerce players.
Planned MFCs of about 40,000-50,000 sq ft; management sees room for MFCs across 50 cities over the next few years.
Delivery partner network grew 31% QoQ, from 2.9 lakh to 3.8 lakh.
demand_pricing: Same-day/next-day Prime delivery is offered across more than 120 cities; management says realization is 15%-20% higher for same-day delivery on the same network.
Customers outside the top 10 are the fastest-growing group; management says the largest customer's share fell by at least 3-4 pp versus its long-term average.
Amazon became a top-5 customer within a year of launch; e-commerce integrations are mostly complete.
Express realization is affected by mix (weight, zones, and Prime's shorter distances), and management expects it to stay in a similar range in the short term.
Management cited a 0% commission model in food delivery as a driver of higher-realization longer-distance orders.

qa_highlights.question: Given the festive season shift to Q3, will guidance be revised upward in the near and medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will wait for Q3 results before revising guidance; the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance is maintained, and it is too early to judge the rest of the sale season.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Hyperlocal realization increase, and how long will it last?
qa_highlights.answer: Realization rose from about INR55 to above INR60, driven by distance and mix: higher on-demand and long-distance orders, plus food delivery growth after the 0% commission model.

qa_highlights.question: What cost build-up hit margins ahead of the season?
qa_highlights.answer: Rental cost rose from 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue (about 30 bps), and depreciation rose slightly. Last-mile and contractual labour scaling had no P&L impact because of the crowdsourced model.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower dependence on the main customer seasonal or strategic?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure fell by at least 3-4 pp from the long-term average this quarter. Management attributes it to strategy (growth in D2C, SME, Prime Large and Hyperlocal), with the enterprise business growing more slowly.

qa_highlights.question: How do MFCs differ from Dark Stores, and is the capex inside the 3.8%-4% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dark Stores deliver in 15-30 minutes; MFCs target 8-12 hour delivery from 40,000-50,000 sq ft sites with 5-10 co-located brands near city-edge sort centres. The capex guidance includes MFCs and Dark Stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Express realizations flat despite more Prime Large and D2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix effects (weight, zones, and shorter-distance Prime orders) offset gains. Realization was marginally up QoQ, marginally down YoY, and is expected to stay in a similar range short term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added services mix and the 2-year outlook for Express versus Hyperlocal?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added services are 35%-40% of revenue and are expected to hold that ratio over 3-5 years. Express and Hyperlocal are not expected to shift materially in mix over the next two years.

Q3 festive-season performance, which will determine whether guidance is revised.

Partner expense rising with Hyperlocal mix; depreciation rising with capex.
Express realization flat YoY; mix shift toward Prime may keep it under pressure.
MFC business is new and capital-heavy, with small revenue expected this year.
Quick commerce competition, although all players are growing.

544695|2026-03.headline: Msafe FY26 revenue rose about 45% to Rs 103.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 39.49% and PAT at Rs 22.02 crore (+72%).
544695|2026-03.overview: Management's first earnings call after IPO reported FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 103.5 crore (up ~45% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 49.9 crore (up ~57%) and PAT of Rs 22.02 crore (up ~72%). EBITDA margin widened to 39.49% from 36.55%, driven by the rental mix and utilisation. Management said MS scaffolding capacity has reached about 6,285 tonnes via temporary rented-premise facilities, ahead of IPO timelines, and entered aluminium formwork. Guidance calls for ~50% CAGR, with the mix shifting toward lower-margin sales, rising capex (~Rs 130 crore) and rising debt.

financial_highlights.change: Increased as yards went from 4 to 18

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 4-5 crore, debt-free (per analyst's figure); analyst also cited ~Rs 38 crore on books

segments.name: Steel (MS) scaffolding
segments.commentary: FY26 total sales plus rental only ~Rs 5 crore. Management guided FY27 to Rs 25-40 crore (5-10x), with steel sales gross margin of ~5-6% and rental yield of 32-38% p.a. Current run-rate cited as ~Rs 1 crore/month rental and ~Rs 1 crore/month sales.

segments.name: Aluminium scaffolding
segments.commentary: ~Rs 98 crore in FY26, roughly split 50-50 sales and rental; current run-rate cited as ~Rs 3 crore/month sales and ~Rs 3.5 crore/month rental. Rental yield 60-66% p.a.; sales gross margin ~30%. Targeted growth ~20% in FY27 core business.

segments.name: Aluminium formwork (new)
segments.commentary: Flagship product launched in FY26; machinery ordered, production targeted by end-June 2026. First-year target Rs 30-40 crore; gross margin guided at ~10% initially, ~15% long term. Management expects at least 30% of revenue from rental.

segments.name: Industrial ladders / safety products
segments.commentary: Ladder manufacturing started, with a proposed channel partner model (none currently). Trading of industrial safety products deferred 3-4 months; no manufacturing planned for those.

guidance_outlook: Management says it expects ~50% CAGR, and later cited a 50-70% CAGR aim; it confirmed FY27 revenue of 'definitely' above Rs 150 crore is achievable but declined to commit to a PAT figure.

IPO proceeds: ~25% used for rental assets by FY26 (rest by 2H FY27); ~11% used for manufacturing and rental expansion, with land acquisition advanced and advanced machines ordered.
demand_pricing: Operating at ~1,000-1,500 sites with ~2,500 customers; pan-India presence versus mostly regional peers; ~20 years of operating experience.
Sales are short-cycle (orders up to 7 days), so aluminium price changes are passed on; rental rates are sticky, so the company absorbs some cost increases.
Aluminium prices reportedly up 40-50%; the company holds large inventory, with a 30% year-end price increase cited, so benefit is not yet fully on the books.
Bad debts under 2% over six years; new customers pay 1-3 months' rental as advance.
Competition: management says there are no entry barriers, with Technocraft cited as a possible entrant in rental and formwork.

qa_highlights.question: Is steel capacity at peak utilisation, and what is the revenue from it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the factory is fully occupied, running around the clock. Steel generates ~Rs 1 crore/month rental and ~Rs 1 crore/month sales, with ~70% of material on rent and 25-30% sold.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~40% EBITDA and ~22% PAT margins sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the mix to change as formwork (mostly sales) and steel grow. The 40% margin may fluctuate slightly, but the company aims to hold the range.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and EBITDA evolve with lower-margin segments growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EBITDA percentage may decline but absolute impact is minimal, and topline growth will offset this. It said its internal targets are much higher than guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex and debt be funded in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex ~Rs 130 crore; funding through debt plus internal accruals, with expected PAT of Rs 30-40 crore. Debt will rise and is typically repaid within 3 years, though debt may be lower if accruals suffice.

qa_highlights.question: Why do customers rent at 32-66% yields rather than buy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited project-based needs, multi-site logistics, capital constraints, and scaffolding being under 1% of project cost. Yields reflect short economic life (aluminium ~5 years vs steel 10-15), with scrap value recoverable.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up to ~Rs 24 crore and ~80 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose from yard expansion (4 to 18), a 30% year-end metal price rise, and precautionary stock; management expects normalisation over time.

Factory-level attrition above 50%, per the call.

544695|2026-06.headline: Msafe Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 40% YoY to ₹31.79 crore and PAT rose 44% to ₹7.27 crore, with the rental business up 24%.
544695|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹31.79 crore (up 40% YoY from ₹22.72 crore), PBT of ₹9.73 crore (up 46% from ₹6.65 crore) and net profit of ₹7.27 crore (up 44% from ₹5.04 crore). The Chairman said MS (formwork/scaffolding) volumes grew 7x YoY via temporary premises, while rental grew 24% and now contributes 46% of revenue. qa_highlights.question: Why has credit cost fallen only gradually despite collection efficiency recovering?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in non-interest income in Q4 and is it sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 3.5%-4% credit cost guidance well above peers despite tighter underwriting?

Q1 is already at the top of the band; guidance could narrow by end-H1.

qa_highlights.question: Fee and other income fell QoQ: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ~INR32-33 crores of decline to no direct assignment in Q1 (DA ~INR20 crores last quarter) and ~INR12 crores FX gain last quarter now moved to OCI, plus lower cross-sell on lower disbursements. Cross-sell insurance income was INR9 crores in Q1.

Opex ratio fell to 8.6% from 8.9% QoQ, and management says NIM is running ahead of guidance partly because a rating upgrade to IND A+ was not factored in. segments.name: Micro-LAP / mortgage
segments.commentary: Mortgage PAR X rose about 1 percentage point over the last quarter to around 6%, still below hypothecation. Management tightened policy and disbursements are being slowed, mainly in parts of MP and Gujarat. Mortgage foreclosures are rising to about 22-23% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Cattle / dairy
segments.commentary: Cattle book is held at roughly 25-28% of AUM, underwritten with a minimum of four to six high-yielding cattle, and static-pool data is described as marginally better than the market. Management does not plan to grow it aggressively.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of reaching the top end of FY27 AUM growth (30%) given the H2 weighting?

544700|2026-03.headline: Fractal Q4 FY26 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR 886 crore (USD 97m) with Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin at 22.1%, while FY26 TMT weakness cut full-year growth to 19%.

FY26 revenue grew 19% to INR 3,300 crore, with management saying TMT client issues cost roughly 8 points of growth (27% ex-TMT). Margins expanded: Q4 gross margin 48.2% and adjusted EBITDA 22.1%, though about 147 bps of Q4 EBITDA came from a UK grant and variable pay true-ups that may not recur. The company repaid its long-term debt after March 31, 2026 using IPO proceeds and is now debt-free.

544700|2026-06.headline: Fractal Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR 912.5 crore (9% constant currency), with TMT down 22% weighing on growth.

Profitability improved: adjusted EBITDA margin rose 189 bps YoY to 16.8%, and net income grew 92% to INR 72 crore (7.9% margin). Management said TMT bottomed and expects sequential growth next quarter, and CFO Ashwath Bhat announced this is his last call. Q1 included a one-month impact of a merit increase effective June 1, with about 120-130 bps full P&L impact expected in Q2.

544700|2026-09.headline: Fractal Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR 957 crore (crossing $100M), with adjusted EBITDA margin at 16.2% and gross margin down 225 bps to 44%.

Adjusted EBITDA grew 30% YoY to a 16.2% margin, while net income rose 139% to INR 79 crore, or INR 102 crore excluding the share of Qure.ai losses. Gross margin fell 225 bps YoY to 44% on investment in forward deployed engineers (FDE) and AI talent ahead of growth, and management expects recovery in Q3 and Q4. Growth was led by HLS (+79%) and BFSI (+30%), with CPG slowing to 11% and TMT returning to sequential growth of 6%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth uneven across verticals (HLS vs CPG), and is it client acceptance or product depth?

qa_highlights.question: Is the gross margin drag an investment in research staff or billable staff?

qa_highlights.question: What are the CPG outlook and G&A trajectory?

qa_highlights.question: What is the partnership and large-deal strategy?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fractal Alpha breakeven path and TMT sustainability?

544711|2026-03.headline: Kiaasa Retail FY26 revenue of ₹134.63 crore, EBITDA margin 17.8% and PAT ₹11.17 crore (+24% YoY); plan of 250 EBOs by 2028.
544711|2026-03.overview: Kiaasa Retail, a Tier 2/3-focused omni-channel women's ethnic wear brand listed on BSE SME in March 2026, reported FY26 revenue from operations of ₹134.63 crore, EBITDA of ₹24 crore (17.8% margin) and net profit of ₹11.17 crore (+24% YoY). Same-store sales growth accelerated to 12.89%, and the company had 124+ active EBOs across 70+ cities as of May 2026. Management attributed margin expansion to sourcing efficiencies and bulk procurement, and laid out a 250-store target by 2028 and 35% revenue CAGR ambition to FY30. Online contribution remains minimal at about 1-2% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 400-500 bps EBITDA margin expansion to 17-18%, and is it sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: How is the shift to Tier 2/3 cities affecting store-level margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 2/3 cities now contribute the most, with consumers willing to pay for affordable luxury; ASP of ₹2,000-2,500 is an aggregate, and the plan is to build footfall first and then raise ASP with new items.

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO proceeds (about ₹46 crore) be deployed and what revenue will follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Proceeds are for store opening only, covering capex and inventory, to open around 66 stores in the next two years; no revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Store sizes, unit economics and capex for new stores; revenue and EBITDA targets for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Current stores are 700-1,000 sq ft; new stores to be around 1,500 sq ft in bigger cities, with some 1,200-1,500 sq ft formats. No EBITDA target given; referred to slide 20 for the FY30 vision of 35% revenue CAGR and EBITDA growth of roughly 45% CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: What share of same-store growth came from volume versus pricing, and why is ASP up while bill value is flat?

qa_highlights.answer: MBO margin for partner is 28-32%, so PAT impact is limited but it adds footfall and awareness. Nine99 stores are cheap, low-rent, single-staff units; no payback period or revenue split was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does the FY30 revenue CAGR of 35% reconcile with FY26 growth of 11.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan includes about 100 more stores beyond 250 by 2030, online growth, and 600-1,000 LFS counters by 2030.

qa_highlights.answer: Online is about 1-2% of revenue today and expected to reach about 10-12% over the next couple of years; no split for FY27 was given.

544717|2026-03.headline: CleanMax FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 28% to INR1,295 crore and PAT to INR86 crore; contracted capacity 5.7 GW with at least 1.5 GW addition guided for FY27.
544717|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue and EBITDA each grew about 28%, with EBITDA at INR1,295 crore against INR1,015 crore, and consolidated PAT rose to about INR86 crore from about INR19 crore. Operational capacity reached 3.1 GW after adding about 1,400 MW, and contracted capacity stood at 5.7 GW including 2.6 GW yet to be executed. Management guided to at least 1,500 MW of RE power sales additions in FY27 but gave no financial guidance. Key new risks raised were Rajasthan CTU curtailment (Bikaner 2 substation at about 30%) and the proposed deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) rules, which management has not yet quantified.

segments.name: RE Power Sales (C&I PPAs)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 3.1 GW plus 2.6 GW contracted and under execution, total 5.7 GW; about 90% of EBITDA, with EBITDA margin 83.5% and gross margin around 92-93%. Average PPA tenor 23.17 years.

segments.name: RE Services (build-own-transfer style)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 555 MW with another 215 MW under construction; EBITDA margin rose to 19.6% from 14.4%. Revenue growth about 28-30% across both segments.

No financial guidance given; management reiterated reported EBITDA has historically been about 1.1x run-rate EBITDA, described as a past pattern rather than a forecast.
Storage/BESS response to DSM and curtailment to be announced in about three to four months.
Management expects EBITDA margin on RE Power Sales to reach nearly 86% in 3-4 years from about 83% today.
Grid forecast for end of Bikaner 2 backdown is September 2026, which management urged investors to treat conservatively.
Net debt to EBITDA target range of 5 to 5.5x; asset-level net debt to EBITDA cited at about 4.3x.
capex_capacity: Added about 1,400-1,471 MW of capacity in FY26 (RE Power Sales plus RE Services) versus less than 500 MW in FY25; operational capacity rose from about 1,700 MW to 3,100 MW in RE Power Sales.
Contracted pipeline of 2.6 GW yet to be executed at start of FY27; management said 100% of capacity expected in FY27 is already contracted.
A 530 MW CTU project at Koppal in Karnataka (450 MW wind, 80 MW solar) is being added in FY27; a 525 MW CTU project in Rajasthan is about 13% of run-rate EBITDA.
Approximately 1 GW of the FY27 additions expected in STU projects.
Solar commissioning planned to be light in July-September 2026 quarter; module deliveries for solar to resume from September or October 2026.
Under construction in Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Uttarakhand, adding new states; currently dispatching power in more than seven states.
demand_pricing: Data and AI customers are 42% of contracted capacity (about 2,400 MW), up from 14% (about 260 MW) on 1 April 2024; named clients include Princeton Digital Group, Iron Mountain, STT Data, and global big tech (Apple, Meta, Google, Amazon per management).
Repeat business was 74% of new volumes contracted in FY26; 82% of volumes are with AA/AAA or MNC clients, 96% with A-rated and above; 588 customers.
Contracted tariff on 2.6 GW under execution averages about INR3.85/unit (about 70% solar, 30% wind, negligible storage).
About 1,600-1,700 MW of the 5.7 GW is contract-for-difference (VPPA/I-REC type) with firm price exposure; management said there is no merchant price exposure on these.
Average PPA tenor 23.17 FY26 (22.73 FY25, 21.54 FY24); average lock-in about 18 years; no client disputes across more than 1,100 contracts.

Management expects module-cost increases from ALMM to pass through to tariffs; customer savings fall from about 30-35% to about 22-25%, with demand still robust; buying accelerated ahead of the June 2026 transition.
Reported grid uptime 99.24% in FY26; wind PLF rose from 32% to 35%, while solar PLF was slightly lower on weaker radiation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Iran war and supply constraints on capex, module costs and interest rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not seen material adverse movement in equipment availability or capital costs attributable to the Iran war, while acknowledging a volatile situation.

qa_highlights.question: Share of under-construction CTU capacity, curtailment exposure and PPA protection?
qa_highlights.answer: The 530 MW Koppal CTU project is mostly wind in South India where curtailment is seen as minimal; PPAs give no protection if the grid curtails, since corporate customers do not pay for performance.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) on revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: No final decision and no internal impact estimate yet; the rules are sub-judice and the government is in talks. Storage is being evaluated to limit DSM downside, with an update in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Nature of INR414 crore pre-tax cash flow hedge gain and negative minority interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge is a balance-sheet fair-value entry on VPPA/I-REC contracts with zero P&L impact given fixed tariffs; minority interest is negative because young SPVs (asset age under two years) carry interest and depreciation before profits.

qa_highlights.question: BESS in the contracted portfolio and tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 5-7 MW of BESS within the 2,600 MW under execution; management would not separate tariffs for storage.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising module prices on IRRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs are expected to adjust to module costs; management said it prices to a constant target IRR, with no expected impact on margins or volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin lower than utility peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Scale and higher SG&A from business development, multi-state offices and 13 MW average PPA size; margin expected to rise to about 86% in 3-4 years, with the 2-3 point gap offset by higher tariffs.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost outlook and Bikaner curtailment timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing may lower costs, but management would not make bold bets given macro risk. Bikaner 2 substation curtailment is about 30%; grid expects end by September 2026 but management urged more conservatism.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 pipeline mix and data-centre share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no reason for the wind/solar mix or the Data and AI share (42% at both start and end of FY26) to change, and says FY27 additions are already fully contracted.

qa_highlights.question: Is run-rate EBITDA adjusted for curtailment, and EBITDA per MW?
qa_highlights.answer: Run-rate EBITDA is not adjusted for curtailment and assumes about 1-1.5% grid downtime; management says per-MW EBITDA is 30-35% higher on a DC basis versus peers using AC.

risks_watch: Rajasthan CTU curtailment: Bikaner 2 at about 30%; management sized impact at about 2.5% of run-rate EBITDA for six months at 40% backdown and about 6.5% for a full year at 50%.
DSM rules: impact not yet quantified; rules are sub-judice, and forecasting improvements are needed industry-wide.
Module cost step-up from ALMM rules from June 2026 and possible timing slippage; solar contracting paused pending government decision.
Rising interest rate environment could offset refinancing benefits; 40% of debt is fixed rate.
Ramp-up of new assets: revenue stabilisation takes three to six months after COD, and the asset-level net debt build-up depends on this.

544717|2026-06.headline: Clean Max Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR55 crore on revenue more than doubling to INR832 crore; FY28 EBITDA guided at minimum INR3,000 crore.
544717|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 107% YoY to INR832 crore, with RE power sales up 47% to INR528 crore and RE services jumping to INR300 crore from INR41 crore. Reported EBITDA rose 68% to INR462 crore (adjusted INR494 crore, up about 74% on a cash basis), and PAT reached INR55 crore. Management added about 500 MW of capacity in the quarter and issued its first FY28 EBITDA guidance of a minimum INR3,000 crore, with steady-state net debt of about INR16,000 crore. Near-term headwinds include a roughly 70% curtailment at the Bikaner CTU project, which management expects to persist through FY27.

vs INR41 crore in prior-year quarter (about 6x)

segments.name: RE power sales
segments.commentary: Revenue INR528 crore, up 47% YoY; EBITDA margin 84% vs 76% a year earlier. Gross margin flat at about 92-93%, with expansion driven by SG&A falling as a share of income. Of total quarterly EBITDA, about INR334 crore came from assets operational for the full prior 12 months.

segments.name: RE services (C&I EPC and O&M)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR300 crore vs INR41 crore a year earlier; EBITDA margin 11.2%. Order book of 147 MW contracted and under execution, with management saying order-to-execution is within 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the deferral of ALMM List-II (cells) and whether the company can benefit.
qa_highlights.answer: Projects commissioned before 31 December can use domestic modules with imported cells, saving about INR60 lakh per MW; company is pulling forward some Maharashtra and Karnataka brownfield STU builds, and no module contract is signed yet.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity by BESS bay for the Koppal CTU project be broken out, and is the March 2027 second bay a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the split on hand; said BESS have spare evacuation capacity and fungibility across the two bays, so a slight delay in the second bay should not break the 1.5 GW target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debenture holders get a security cover change from 0.7x to 1x?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the trust deed allowed a range of 0.7x to 1.25x; the company fixed it at 1x for consistency with the planned corporate bond, not an increase.

qa_highlights.question: Battery storage: how it plays into business and whether new PPAs include batteries.
qa_highlights.answer: Company has greenlit a first BESS STU project in Rajasthan, signed MOUs with three clients in the last month, and sees three C&I use cases; BESS-as-a-Service tariff uplift estimated at INR3-4/unit excluding generation cost.

qa_highlights.question: Curtailment impact on EBITDA and quarterly generation/PLF detail.
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates the Bikaner CTU project is 13% of run-rate EBITDA; at 70% curtailment that is about INR170 crore on a full-year basis; EBITDA would be about 8-9% higher without it. PLF given on trailing 12 months basis only.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from Adani, Reliance and NTPC entering C&I, and why hyperscalers keep choosing CleanMax.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 15 years of C&I focus, 600+ customers with 80% of new volume from repeat clients, multi-state wind-plus-solar footprint, and a fragmented market where it holds about 14% share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3,000 crore FY28 EBITDA guidance corporate-level, and what is the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is corporate-level, including RE services; steady-state net debt corresponding to INR3,000 crore EBITDA is about INR16,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of growth: can the company repeat contracted capacity growth of about 4,000 MW over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can meet or exceed about 4,000 MW of contracted additions over two years, but tripling is not feasible given execution limits; organisational gaps in five to six areas were reviewed with the board.

544718|2026-03.headline: PNGS Reva FY26 revenue rose 70% to INR439 crore and Q4 revenue rose 139% to INR138 crore, though FY26 PAT grew only 9% to INR65 crore.
544718|2026-03.overview: PNGS Reva reported its first full standalone year (FY26) as a separate entity, with revenue from operations of INR439 crore (up 70% on restated FY25) and EBITDA of INR95 crore at a 22% margin. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR138 crore (up 139% YoY), with EBITDA of INR31 crore (22% margin) and PAT of INR21 crore (16% margin). Management attributed the margin dilution versus the earlier divisional period to standalone costs such as rent, inventory and logistics, and CEO/CFO/compliance functions. Management guided to 25-30% SSG and top-line growth in FY27-28, with 15 new stores over 24 months funded from IPO proceeds. Around INR55-60 crore of FY26 revenue was surplus gold received as consideration, per management.

qa_highlights.answer: SIS commission is about 4% of sales blended, none on gold; FY26 SSG about 40%. EBO target is about INR9 crore revenue at 0.75x turn (about 2.5-3 customers a day at INR1.2 lakh bill), about INR1.5 crore EBITDA initially, rising to INR3-3.5 crore in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from around 30-32% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone costs such as separate premises rent, inventory and logistics department, and CEO, CFO and compliance functions were not borne by the division earlier. Management says these costs now load the P&L and sustain a lower EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is 28% gross margin and 22% EBITDA margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin can rise as brand value is loaded into diamond pricing; currently no brand premium is charged, and the industry runs 30-35% or up to 40-42% gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will gold price rises affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin percentage may contract as gold share rises, but management expects rupee gross profit to be maintained or grow.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to surplus gold received in exchanges?
qa_highlights.answer: It is received as consideration and sold in the open market or B2B to avoid working capital being stuck; inventory is valued at average purchase price, so no inventory gain is booked.

qa_highlights.question: Will inventory turn fall as 6-7 new EBOs open in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 1.31x to be maintained because new EBOs at about 0.75x are offset by SIS SSG; it says a fall would be limited to between 1.25x and 1.35x.

qa_highlights.question: How will growth capex be funded post-IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals (about INR64 crore FY26 earnings retained), with INR150-200 crore of unused sanctioned debt; no equity dilution expected, and borrowing expansion planned after 2030.

544720|2026-06.headline: Omnitech Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 61.5% YoY to INR166.6 crore and PAT rose 468.7% to INR29.73 crore, with management guiding 35–40% YoY growth.
544720|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 61.5% YoY to INR166.6 crore, EBITDA rose 90.8% to INR50.62 crore, and PAT reached INR29.73 crore. Net working capital days fell to 233 from 294 at FY26-end, driven mainly by lower inventory and receivable days. Management reiterated an order book above INR3,000 crore and a two-facility capex programme of about INR250 crore at Chhapara. Net debt to equity rose to 0.41x from 0.34x, and cash fell to INR133.75 crore from INR163 crore.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: About 49% of Q1 revenue, down from about 52.7% in Q4 FY26. Pure oil and gas is below 40% of revenue per management.

segments.name: Motion control and automation
segments.commentary: About 24% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Industrial equipment systems
segments.commentary: About 19% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Others / diversified industrial applications
segments.commentary: About 6.9% of Q1 revenue, which management linked to early revenue from defence and aerospace first articles.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guided at about 35–40% YoY for FY28 (management said FY27/FY28 framing was on a YoY basis).
EBITDA margin guided at 30% and above.
Gross margin currently around 70%; management estimates a range of 68% to 71%.
Net working capital days target: a further 10–20% improvement, with historical levels below 200–220 days cited as the reference.
Two new facilities at Chhapara to be operationalised within about 14 months; the new Chhapara facility is expected to start commercial operations in FY28.
Depreciation moved from written-down value to straight-line method, expected to continue in coming quarters.
Defence and aerospace revenue expected over 1–3 years; some revenue expected in FY27 and more in FY28.
capex_capacity: Annualised machine-hour capacity is about 31–32 lakh hours across three plants: Metoda about 11 lakh, existing Chhapara about 19.5 lakh, Padavala about 1.37 lakh (as stated).
Capex of about INR250 crore for two new facilities at Chhapara: about INR100 crore buildings and INR150 crore plant and machinery, of which about INR25 crore is for existing Chhapara capacity.
Post-capex capacity is estimated at 42–43 lakh machine hours; capacity to be added in stages as machines are installed.
Some spillover of capex into FY28 is expected because of rain, with projects running about 1–1.5 months behind schedule.
Land acquired in Ahmedabad and Hyderabad; no capex plan yet for these sites. Management said debt of INR390 crore remains after INR50 crore of IPO-funded repayment.
A 1.2 MW solar plant funded from IPO capex has started generating power.
demand_pricing: Order book is above INR3,000 crore as of 31 July 2026, including a multi-year Weatherford order exceeding USD100 million. About INR2,000 crore relates to two large orders with 3–5 year execution, and about INR1,000 crore is short- to moderate-cycle (6–18 months).

Geographic mix in Q1: North America 52%, Asia 27%, India 17%, Europe/UK 3%; exports about 78% of revenue. Management expects North America at 55–60% of the order book, with Middle East and Europe growing.

Management said raw-material cost changes are passed to customers through pass-through mechanisms and quarterly business reviews, with a lag of about 2–3 months; it also cited forex pass-through. It said 100% pass-through.
Existing facilities can generate about INR800–900 crore of annual revenue, per management.
Asset turnover of about 2–2.5x and ROCE above 20% expected over time, per management.
Nadcap accreditation is in progress and defence/aerospace first articles are underway; approvals may take 6–15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are machine-hour capacities by site, and what is the capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is about 31–32 lakh hours; the INR250 crore capex (INR100 crore building, INR150 crore plant) takes this to 42–43 lakh hours, with about INR25 crore of the machinery for existing Chhapara.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and timing of the large-order execution from the two anchor orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution has started, with an expected run-rate of about INR50 crore and more, ramping over years one to five; short-cycle industrial orders of about 3–4 months are also being executed.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be assessed for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projected 35–40% growth and EBITDA margin of 30% and above, and said margins are capability-driven with product-level variation of 1–2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material cost rise sequentially and what is the pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed changes to product mix in a low-volume, high-mix business and to a 2–3 month lag tied to quarterly reviews; it said pass-through is 100%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scalable revenue potential from the new capex and what ROCE should be assumed?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing plants can do about INR800–900 crore a year. New capacity will be added in stages; management expects asset turnover of 2–2.5x and ROCE above 20% at peak, though this takes years.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further working capital improvement, and what is the order-book geographic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a further 10–20% improvement, citing minimum MOQ needs for new vertical first articles. North America is 55–60% of the order book, with Middle East and Europe making up 10–20%.

risks_watch: Capex spillover into FY28 and about 1–1.5 months of schedule delay due to rain.
Working capital remains elevated at 233 days, and management said MOQ needs for new FAs may keep inventory high.
Net debt to equity rose to 0.41x and cash fell by about INR29 crore quarter-end to quarter-end (from INR163 crore to INR133.75 crore).
Sequential raw-material cost increase (transcript cites 20%, 24%, then 28%) and the 2–3 month pass-through lag.
Defence and aerospace approvals (Nadcap, FA) are not complete and timing is uncertain.
Revenue concentration: energy is 49% of revenue and 78% of revenue is exports; North America is 52%.

But we are right on track as far as the FA approvals are concerned and also the process which are in line for us to get approved.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 35-40% YoY revenue growth, backed by execution of two anchor orders at about INR50 cr run-rate ramping over years one to five, and about INR1,000 cr of short-cycle (6-18 months) orders within the INR3,000 cr+ book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The INR250 cr two-facility programme is already committed, so a fresh announcement is not needed; utilisation is about flat at 31-32 lakh hours, not clearly at 80%+ stress, and land in Ahmedabad and Hyderabad has no capex plan yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book above INR3,000 cr as of 31 July 2026 (incl. multi-year Weatherford order above USD100 mn) and Q1 revenue +61.5% YoY, but guidance is a 35-40% YoY range for FY28, with no near-term raise signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Capex running 1-1.5 months behind schedule because of rain, working capital still at 233 days, net debt/equity up to 0.41x from 0.34x, and defence/aerospace approvals (Nadcap, FA) may take 6-15 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Defence and aerospace first articles are underway with some revenue expected in FY27 and more in FY28, though Nadcap approval timing is uncertain (6-15 months); Others segment was 6.9% of Q1 revenue.

rows.label: Anchor orders ramp (INR2,000 cr over 3-5 years)
rows.why: About INR2,000 cr relates to two large orders with 3-5 year execution, execution has started with an expected run-rate of about INR50 cr and more, and about INR1,000 cr is short-cycle (6-18 months).

rows.label: Further working-capital release
rows.why: NWC days fell from 294 to 233 (target a further 10-20% improvement, reference below 200-220 days), but management said MOQ needs for new FAs may keep inventory high (inventory days 182 vs 225 at FY26-end).

rows.why: Management claims 100% pass-through with a 2-3 month lag, but raw-material cost rose sequentially (cited 20%, 24%, then 28%), so near-term gross margin could compress before pass-through catches up.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the INR3,000 cr+ order book and Chhapara capacity, but cautious and evasive on margin drivers, the raw-material lag, FA/defence approval timing and the rise in net debt to equity to 0.41x.

544720|2026-09.headline: Omnitech Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.5% YoY to INR175.56 crore; H1 revenue up 50% and order book about INR3,178 crore.
544720|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue grew 40.5% YoY to INR175.56 crore, with EBITDA up 17.7% to INR51.25 crore and PAT up 35.5% to INR30.57 crore, so margins compressed. H1 FY27 revenue rose 50% YoY, with PBT up 117.3% to INR80.01 crore. Management guided full-year FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and EBITDA margin of 30-32%, and said the Chhapara expansion is due in about 10-11 months. The call also covered new defence, aerospace and data-centre order flow, but several answers on capacity and timing were loose.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: 53.5% of Q2 revenue and 76% of order book; management described the business as mainly operations and maintenance rather than capex-linked.

segments.name: Motion control and automation
segments.commentary: 22.9% of Q2 revenue and about 12% of order book.

segments.name: Industrial equipment systems
segments.commentary: 19.4% of Q2 revenue and about 11.5% of order book.

segments.name: Other diversified applications
segments.commentary: 4.2% of Q2 revenue; new data-centre and defence work sits in this and adjacent mix, with first commercial orders received.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% YoY; management said 40% would be welcome but is not the current estimate.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 30-32%; management cited a historical 30-33% range to sustain over about 3 years.
Q3 and Q4 margins expected to be in line with a 32-33% historical range for the full year (answer on profitability, which is ambiguous).
Order book expected to convert over about 5 years (Weatherford programme), with FY28 ramp-up and larger contribution in FY29-FY30.
Chhapara expansion to complete in about 10-11 months (behind schedule by 1-2 months); peak revenue potential stated at INR1,100-1,200 crore on about 2x asset turn.
Average borrowing cost around 8-8.25%; about INR210 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised, to be deployed on schedule.
capex_capacity: Annualised machine-hour capacity at Sept 30, 2026 was 3.34 million hours, up 26.2% from 2.65 million hours in FY26.
Current utilisation stated at about 68-71%; peak utilisation of 80-85% considered achievable.
Chhapara, Rajkot expansion under construction; commissioning in about 10-11 months.
IPO capex of INR418 crore: INR50 crore debt repayment done, about INR208 crore utilised, about INR210 crore unutilised.
Further capex of INR1,200 crore-scale considered for next 2-3 years from debt and internal accruals; Gujarat Viksit scheme being explored for funding.
demand_pricing: Approximately 89% of Q2 revenue from outside India; North America 65.5%, Asia 20.9%, India 10.8%, Europe and UK 2.8%.

Order book about INR3,178 crore as of Oct 31, 2026; mix of 1-3 year orders and a 5-year Weatherford programme; management indicated roughly INR600 crore a year as an oversimplification and said ramp-up would be gradual.
Raw material and currency movements are passed through to customers under contracts with a 5-8% band, reviewed quarterly or half-yearly; cancellation not part of the discussion for these orders.
Data-centre qualification takes 8-14 months; management said margins in data-centre work will not differ from current levels.
Aerospace and defence: first-article orders executed and approved; commercial production orders received; NADCAP certification in progress; in-house metallurgical lab NABL accredited under ISO 17025.
Q2 other expenses rose as a share of sales (about 28% per analyst) due to tooling, consumables, heat-treatment job work and new-capacity ramp-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 other expense increase as a share of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher tooling and consumables usage, job work such as heat treatment, and costs linked to new capacity ramp-up and new machines; expected to normalise over FY27 as Q3 and Q4 ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating leverage as it enters data-centre, defence and new segments, plus raw-material MOQ constraints and new product development; it expects a 30-33% historical margin range to hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential from Chhapara capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak revenue of about INR1,100-1,200 crore could be reached, based on roughly 2x asset turn and 30-35% growth; it declined the analyst's INR1,400-1,500 crore figure.

qa_highlights.question: How was the INR3,178 crore order book expected to convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders run from 1 to 5 years; dispatches begin this year and ramp through FY28, with larger volumes in FY29 and FY30 as new capacity commissions.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the IPO proceeds are used?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR418 crore IPO objects, INR50 crore went to debt repayment and about INR208 crore is utilised in total, with about INR210 crore still unutilised.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for a dedicated facility for end customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said discussions are ongoing with large OEMs but are too preliminary to disclose; it will only announce once confirmed.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin fell to the 29-30% range in recent quarters versus the historical 35-40% cited by an analyst; watch whether the 30-32% FY27 range holds.
Sequential slowdown: analyst cited QoQ revenue growth of 5.3% and PAT growth of 2.8%.
Chhapara expansion timeline has already slipped 1-2 months; any further delay affects FY28 ramp-up.
Data-centre and defence qualification cycles of 8-14 months and NADCAP timing could defer revenue.
Other expenses elevated as a share of sales; management expects normalisation in H2 FY27 but has not quantified it.
Management answers on IPO fund deployment, EBITDA-margin basis and H1 PAT figures were imprecise; verify against the financial results filing.

544723|2026-09.headline: Sedemac Q2 FY27 revenue grew over 40% to a record, but EBITDA margin dipped on raw material inflation; H2 EBITDA guided to hold versus H1.
544723|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 and H1 FY27 revenue, each up more than 40% year on year, with Q2 revenue of roughly Rs 400 crore. EBITDA margin declined on raw material cost inflation, partly offset by operating leverage. Management expects H2 EBITDA to hold at H1 levels despite further PCB cost pressure, with price corrections and the new ISG controller as offsets. The MF3 plant has begun pilot production, and H2 capex is guided lower than H1.

544731|2026-09.headline: Rajputana Stainless Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR360 crore and PAT 79% to INR23.7 crore, with operating cash flow weak at INR4.5 crore in H1.

544733|2026-06.overview: Revenue was broadly stable at INR386 crore versus INR377 crore in the prior-year quarter, with strong domestic momentum partly offset by raw material constraints in international business. Gross margin improved on a richer mix of specialty and patented products, and EBITDA was stated at around 11%. PAT rose almost 16% to INR26.4 crore, but management said about INR5.7 crore of other income came from a land sale, which is a one-off. Management targets a domestic market share rise from about 3-3.5% to 7-8%.

Management says patented product share of the portfolio will double in 2-3 years, with about 12 products launched in the last 3 years and two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year.

544735|2026-03.headline: Novus Loyalty FY26 revenue rose about 22% to ~127 Cr, with PAT of ~9.28 Cr (7.29% margin) in its first results call after its 25 March 2026 listing.

EBITDA was about 12.33 Cr (9.68% margin) and PAT about 9.28 Cr (7.29% margin), with management citing PAT growth of about 150% and EBITDA growth of about 120%. Management attributed margin improvement to programs maturing (redemptions rising in years 2 to 3) and a shift toward technology and merchant-promotion revenue, which carry no direct procurement cost. Management guided to growth above 20% in FY27 and to international revenue at least doubling, but gave no formal numerical guidance, and the call was largely promotional with limited hard data.

544741|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.5% to INR16.11 crore and PAT rose 66.9% to INR4.10 crore, with management guiding FY27 revenue of INR30-32 crore.
544741|2026-03.overview: Highness Microelectronics reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) as its strongest year since listing on BSE SME: revenue INR16.11 crore (+14.5% YoY), EBITDA INR6.61 crore (+46%), and PAT INR4.10 crore (+66.9%). Management attributed margin gains to favourable project mix and high-margin contracts, and said H2 has historically been stronger than H1. Growth plans centre on a Goa facility for COG/FOG display manufacturing, a glass cutting line at Rabale, and an MoU with Axiom (USA). Management did not give a clean H2 standalone revenue figure, and several answers on order book and margins were loosely quantified.

544741|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 63.4% to INR12.01 crores and PAT rose 167% to INR2.47 crores, but operating cash flow was negative INR14.58 crores.
544741|2026-09.overview: Highness Microelectronics reported H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) revenue from operations of INR12.01 crores, up from INR7.35 crores, with operating EBITDA of INR3.85 crores (32.1% margin) and PAT of INR2.47 crores (20.6% margin). Growth was driven by lower COGS growth (about 3%) against revenue growth, though employee costs rose to 21.7% of revenue. Net operating cash outflow was INR14.58 crores, driven by supplier advances, a fall in payables and receivables of INR13.73 crores, which management attributed to timing and to long credit terms given to two export customers. Management announced the Goa Fast Track project, a leased-space line for an energy-sector customer seeking local content under PLI, and said an MoU for at least three years is near signing.

qa_highlights.question: Given the many parallel initiatives (Noumed integration, capacity, R&D, US entry), how is management bandwidth protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Anil K K said Sai is retaining the existing Noumed management, which holds 25.4% of Noumed, and the 4 senior Prathyak managers, with Sai providing manufacturing, funding and procurement support.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire 60% of a new facility rather than upgrade Jeedimetla as originally planned?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 margin decline from Noumed a one-off, and is the guidance upgrade possible?

544742|2026-09.headline: Sai Parenterals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9% QoQ to INR196.1 crore, with gross margin up to 47.5% and EBITDA margin to 21.1%.

Gross margin improved from 40.9% to 47.5% as raw material cost fell about 3% on tighter inventory controls, lifting EBITDA 67% QoQ to INR41.4 crore (21.1% margin). Depreciation rose to INR25.1 crore from INR8.1 crore on Noumed and Sai Prathyak asset capitalisation, but PAT still grew 33% QoQ to INR10.5 crore. Management reclassified other income below EBITDA, restating Q1 EBITDA to INR24.7 crore (13.7%). Acquisitions of 60% in Saicriti Pharma and Sai Prathyak Laboratories closed, and the Adelaide and Unit III projects are moving towards operation.

qa_highlights.question: Amol Rao (Plutus Wealth): Why did receivables rise to about INR250 crore in H1, and what is the ageing?

The Q2 build reflected lower collections from two large export customers and sales bunched in the last 1-1.5 months. Domestic ageing to be below 120 days within two to three quarters.

544750|2026-03.headline: Om Power Transmission Q4 FY26 revenue rose 67.2% YoY to INR 174.62 crores; FY26 order book hit a record INR 621 crores.

544750|2026-09.headline: Om Power Transmission Q2 FY27 revenue rose 56% to INR 128.29 crore, EBITDA margin 15.25%, order book about INR 839 crore after October wins.
544750|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 128.29 crore (+56% YoY) and H1 was INR 249.93 crore (+46%), with PAT of INR 13.85 crore for the quarter (+117% YoY). EBITDA margin of 15.25% was above the company's steady-state range, which management attributed to segment and project mix plus the specialised Dholera fast-track work. Order inflow picked up sharply after quarter end, with INR 273.21 crore of October wins taking the order book to about INR 839 crore before October execution. Receivables rose to INR 237.06 crore, largely retention from projects in advanced execution, while trade payables fell, driving negative operating cash flow of INR 38.20 crore for H1.

segments.name: Substation
segments.commentary: Contributed 17% of H1 and Q2 FY27 revenue; the 400 kV GIS substation at Dholera was commissioned and is described as a credential for future GIS orders.

segments.name: Underground cabling
segments.commentary: Share of the order book was low earlier; new orders from PGVCL (11 kV, Bhavnagar), two GETCO 66 kV orders, and UGVCL (Ambaji, October) have restored it as a meaningful part of the book. Margins are lower than EHV transmission lines.

segments.name: Operation and maintenance (O&M)
segments.commentary: Manpower-supply vertical fell to 3% of H1 revenue, which management linked to lower employee cost; O&M carries lower EBITDA margin and will be bid only where margins are acceptable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 50% YoY; management reiterated this when asked about a higher run-rate path toward INR 720-730 crore.
Order book expected at INR 1,000-1,200 crore by fiscal year end, per Fenil Patel.
Long-term EBITDA margin band of about 12-13% and PAT margin of 8-9% on a yearly basis; management said 14-15% would be optimistic as a steady state, though a quarter can run higher on mix.
FY30 revenue target of about INR 2,500 crore, tied to entry into 765 kV tenders from GETCO and Power Grid and GIS substation orders.
Borrowing cost guided at 9-10% currently, expected to move toward about 8% as the CRISIL rating improves (cited as BBB+).
Dholera Package 2 to be completed by December 2026 and Package 3 by March 2027.
capex_capacity: Order book of about INR 839 crore after October 2026 wins of INR 273.21 crore, against INR 565.99 crore at 30 Sep 2026; about 1.9x FY26 revenue before October execution.

Investment property rose from INR 3 crore to INR 5 crore; management said it is a rented commercial property added to build collateral for bank guarantees.
demand_pricing: GETCO tender flow was slow at the start of FY27 and picked up in September and October with a strong flow of awards.
Gujarat Wire-Free City Mission aims to convert overhead distribution networks in municipal areas to underground cabling by 2030, with an initial INR 500 crore provision for phase 1.
Bid pipeline of about INR 1,600 crore, which management expects to convert into orders in 3-4 months; it includes 765 kV bids for both Power Grid and GETCO.

Management said competition has compressed O&M margins over time.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins of 14-15% be sustained in H2, and what drove Q2 margin uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the annual EBITDA range is 12-13% and PAT 8-9%; the Q2 uplift came from transmission line mix (79%) and the specialised Dholera fast-track job, with quarterly results depending on project mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen to about 45% of revenue, and what is the collection plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Modi said receivables are high because most projects are in their last three to four billing stages, so retention (about 45% of receivables) has built up and is expected to normalise on project closure.

qa_highlights.question: Why is finance cost rising while borrowings fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost includes bank guarantee commission on the 10% performance guarantees required on GETCO contracts, which scale with top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY30 vision and what revenue and margin targets are set?
qa_highlights.answer: Fenil Patel said FY30 revenue is targeted at about INR 2,500 crore, supported by 765 kV and GIS participation; management declined to give a margin target beyond the 12-13% band.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 237 crore receivables is over six months old?
qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Modi said 84% of debtors fall in the under-6-months ageing bucket, which includes not-due retention as well as regular billing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be able to fully execute 765 kV orders alone?
qa_highlights.answer: Fenil Patel said Om Power would be individually qualified for upcoming GETCO 765 kV tenders without a JV.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivables at INR 237 crore (about 45% retention) and negative H1 operating cash flow of INR 38.20 crore; management guided to positive cash flow but gave no date.

Concentration: order wins and execution remain largely with GETCO and Gujarat utilities; the first tender wins outside Gujarat are still pending.

Dholera Package 2 and 3 completion (December 2026 and March 2027) and execution of the INR 621 crore unexecuted book, which management said would complete by June 2027.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables of INR 237.06 crore (about 45% retention), H1 operating cash flow of negative INR 38.20 crore, and Dholera Package 2 and 3 completion dates (December 2026, March 2027) create execution and cash risk to the 50% growth guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Entry into 765 kV tenders from GETCO and Power Grid (Om Power to bid individually, without a JV) and GIS substation orders underpin the INR 2,500 crore FY30 revenue target, but no dated launch was given and 765 kV projects take 24-36 months.

rows.label: October wins lift order book to about INR 839 crore
rows.why: INR 273.21 crore of October wins took the order book from INR 565.99 crore at 30 Sep 2026 to about INR 839 crore, about 1.9x FY26 revenue before October execution.

544754|2026-03.headline: Kissht (OnEMI) FY26 AUM rose 73% YoY to ₹7,066 crore; GNPA fell to 2.12% and FY26 PAT grew 75% to ₹281 crore.
544754|2026-03.overview: First earnings call since the May 8, 2026 listing. AUM grew 19% QoQ to ₹7,066 crore and PAT grew 52% YoY and 7% QoQ in Q4. Asset quality improved, with GNPA down 77 bps YoY to 2.12% and Stage-3 ECL coverage at 86.2%. Management deliberately reduced yields to target higher-quality borrowers, which compressed the Q3-to-Q4 margin, and guided to FY27 AUM growth above 40%, ROA of 4.5-5% and ROE of 19-21%.

segments.name: Personal loans (unsecured, on-book and off-book)
segments.commentary: On-book AUM ₹3,556 crore and off-book AUM ₹3,510 crore, with off-book covered by FLDG capped at 5%. Disbursements were cut about 7% and about 450 pin codes were paused on early-warning flags.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹518 crore across 98 branches in 8 states, or 7.3% of AUM. LTV is about 48% and expected to stay range-bound. LAP is not yet at breakeven and is about 1-2 years from steady-state ROA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth above 40%, with secured book scale-up expected to be strong.
Gross NPA below 2.25%, impairment costs down 10-15% YoY, and continued Stage-1 mix improvement.
Return on average AUM of 4.5-5%, which implies ROE of 19-21%. Guidance is for FY27 alone.
Yield is expected to keep declining over the next four to six quarters at a pace similar to Q3-to-Q4. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term and 14-16% in three to four quarters.
Cost of borrowing fell about 200 bps after the Crisil A- upgrade in February 2026; a further upgrade in FY27 could cut it another 100-150 bps in FY28.
LAP: at least 80 more branches by end of FY27, with calibrated expansion in Karnataka, AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, UP and Maharashtra.
No disbursement guidance for FY27; guidance is on AUM growth.
capex_capacity: IPO proceeds: 75% of primary issue (about ₹630 crore) already infused as equity into NBFC subsidiary Si Creva Capital; balance 25% for general corporate purposes including technology, AI, brand and customer acquisition.
Capital position described as comfortable for 40% AUM growth in FY27; no near-term fundraise indicated.
Collections team expanded in Q4 FY26, mainly on the field side, with a dedicated NPA recovery team. Operating base: over 7,000 field agents and 1,000+ tele-callers.
Steady-state on-book debt-to-equity seen at 2.5-3x; off-book leverage not a constraint since only the 5% FLDG is blocked.
New wholly-owned subsidiary created to distribute mutual funds and wealth products.
demand_pricing: Margin compression is deliberate: yields reduced to win higher-quality, lower-risk borrowers, with benefits from operating leverage and lower funding costs partly passed to customers.
Repeat customers: 11.76 million unique customers to date, about 3.5 million active; repeat share supports growth.
Acquisition: digital marketing under 50% of acquisition, partner channels (merchants, e-commerce, aggregators) about 55%, organic about 30%.
Competition cited as Bajaj and Chola; management points to credit performance and repeat-customer base as edge.
Borrowing cost on-book ranged 11.5%-14.25% across 45+ lenders.

qa_highlights.question: Rating upgrade outlook and impact on borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Crisil rated A- in Feb 2026 and India Ratings A- in Nov 2025. About 200 bps lower marginal cost of borrowing already seen since the Crisil upgrade. Another upgrade is possible in FY27 (discussion over next 6-8 months), worth a further 100-150 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA so much higher than two years ago (0.79% to 2.89%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a technical change: the write-off period was extended from 120 to 150 days after discussion with auditors. GNPA has been stable on the 150-day basis for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 OPEX rise and other income fall?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP not yet at breakeven and branch additions; plus a one-time Q4 investment in field collections staff for FY27 recoveries. Other income fell sequentially with a small margin compression.

qa_highlights.question: What is the portfolio yield and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 portfolio yield about 30-31%, 50-75 bps below Q3. Management expects a similar downward trend for four to six quarters. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is FLDG capped at 5% and can lenders push IRR above it?
qa_highlights.answer: Contractual risk is capped at 5% FLDG. Lenders may negotiate on hurdle rates, but the exposure does not extend beyond the FLDG.

qa_highlights.question: How is AUM growth changing the ROA and secured-mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall AUM growth above 40%. The 4.5% ROA guidance covers the whole book, with secured lending at lower ROA. Management expects secured to reach roughly 19-21% ROE over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP and AUM growth accelerate QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting higher-quality customers at lower rates, plus repeat customers from the 3.5 million active base. Management says April-May momentum continues.

risks_watch: Yield compression is guided to continue for four to six quarters; ROA of 4.5-5% depends on funding-cost and opex offsets.
LAP is loss-making at the margin and needs 1-2 years to reach steady-state ROA; 80 new branches add opex.
Stage-3 and gross NPA trends depend on the 150-day write-off policy; a change in policy would shift the reported number.
Off-book book depends on FLDG partner appetite and on negotiated lender hurdle rates.
Rating upgrade and resulting funding-cost cuts are not assured; timing depends on FY27 rating reviews.
544754|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and guidance, with explicit emphasis on prudence and ROA protection. Cautious on near-term margins, which management openly says will keep declining. Evasive on disbursement targets and on the exact origination yield for April-May.
key_quotes: And at this stage, we believe, Prudence ceases to be a conservative instinct - it becomes a genuine competitive advantage.
We would rather carry prudence slightly early than discover optimism slightly late.
Kissht is a technology company that does lending - not the other way around, a lending company that uses technology.

We are not building for the next quarter, rather, we are building for the next decade - with sharper judgments, stronger governance, deeper technology, and a balance sheet designed to compound through cycles, not merely benefit from favorable ones.

544754|2026-06.headline: Kissht Q1 FY27: PAT rose 59% YoY to INR 95 crore and AUM 61% YoY to INR 8,001 crore, with credit cost down to 6.80% of average AUM.
544754|2026-06.overview: Management reported AUM of INR 8,001 crore (+61% YoY, +13% QoQ) and PAT of INR 95 crore (+59% YoY, +16% QoQ), with ROAA at 5.05% and ROAE at 21.20%. Credit cost fell to 6.80% of average AUM from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26. Total income as a share of average AUM fell 249 bps QoQ, which management attributed to deliberate pricing for higher-quality customers and a rise in off-book share from 49.7% to 53.6%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance (AUM growth of 40%+, 15% credit cost reduction, ROA of 5%+ and ROE of 20%+) and said it is on track.

segments.name: Personal loans (PL)
segments.commentary: Customer rate about 29-30%; including processing fees, bounce and penal charges, and insurance income, effective yield about 36-37%. Management said PL is the core growth engine.

segments.commentary: Subsidiary has received AMFI registration. Management described this as a fee-income line; no size or timing was given.

Management committed to ROA of 5%+ and ROE of 20%+ consistently. It described a three-year plan to pass through about 8-9% of revenue margin while holding ROA.
Possible credit rating upgrades from India Ratings and CRISIL under discussion; management said any upgrade would affect FY28 borrowing costs more than FY27.
capex_capacity: LAP scaled to 101 branches in eight states; management said it adds branches almost every quarter.
Capital raised through the May 2026 IPO of about INR 850 crore; NBFC capital adequacy rose to 40.2%.

Technology: underwriting uses 7,200+ signals; AUC of the model is 74% (66% in 2023); more than 7,000 field agents and 1,000+ tele-callers; over 95% of collections handled in-house; more than 80% of own code written with AI.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the fall in revenue margin to the higher share of lower-priced repeat, high-quality customers and the rise in off-book share, which earns a servicing fee instead of interest income.

Tightened underwriting for salaried applicants without recent EPFO credits and for self-employed borrowers with weaker banking credit. Approval band was moved to 3.7 from 4 in specific segments; management is reviewing this.
Management said bureau data shows stress in small-ticket loans and multi-lender borrowers at industry level, but its own post-December 2025 vintages are performing better.
Management said July collections improved versus June, and that Q1 seasonality in bounce rates should reverse in July-September.

qa_highlights.question: What drove AUM growth this quarter and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited model-driven approvals of a high share of good-quality customers, plus reopening some previously paused pin codes; it said the growth is sustainable for the foreseeable future.

qa_highlights.question: Can AUM growth exceed the 40%+ guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranvir Singh said 13% QoQ growth already in Q1 means the company expects to over-deliver on the 40%+ 12-month AUM growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Pin-code pause status: how many were paused now versus last quarter, and how does this square with higher bounce and slightly lower collection efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Of about 11,000 pin codes contributing 98% of business (out of 17,000 served), 450 were paused in Q4 FY26; 180 were reopened and 270 remain paused. Management cited credit cost falling to 6.80% from 7.02% and said Q1 bounce seasonality should reverse in July-September, with July collections better than June.

qa_highlights.question: Yield and cost of funds: PL vs LAP yield, incremental cost of funds, and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PL customer rate 29-30%, effective yield 36-37% including fees; LAP yield 16% to 23-24%, average about 21.8%. One Q1 raise carried a loaded cost of about 12.9%, about 150 bps below FY26 average borrowing cost; reported 4.45% AUM-level cost moved to daily-average basis (about 10 bps better). Cost of borrowing expected to fall at least 100 bps over three quarters, mainly H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Share of organic sourcing and medium-term yield/ROA bridge?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic channel share rose to 31% in Q1 from 27% in Q4 and about 23-24% average in FY26, with a target of 40-50%. Over three years management sees about 4-5% benefit from operating leverage, 200-300 bps from lower cost of funds, and risk reduction, totalling about 8-9% of revenue margin passed through while holding ROA at 5%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry stress signal and how has underwriting changed for specific profiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry bureau data shows stress in recent sourcing; its own post-December 2025 sourcing is performing better. It tightened salaried applicants lacking recent EPFO credits (now using account aggregator data) and self-employed borrowers with weaker banking credit, and approval band was moved to 3.7 from 4 in specific segments, now under review.

qa_highlights.question: LAP profitability, branch breakeven, and LAP ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP breakeven expected around Q3 FY27; branch breakeven takes about 7-8 months versus 16-18 months for an average branch, with over 40% of LAP customers from the PL base. LAP ROE target is 20%+, with no separate ROA figure given.

risks_watch: Revenue margin compression: total income fell 249 bps of average AUM QoQ, with off-book share rising to 53.6%; watch whether PPOP and PAT keep growing as the margin falls.

FLDG accounting: the 5% upfront FLDG is blocked capital, and utilised FLDG sits in credit cost or opex; the Q1 FLDG opex amount was not disclosed (Krishnan estimated about 1%).
LAP breakeven (around Q3 FY27) and the new mutual fund distribution line (AMFI registration only; no size or timing) are still unproven.

544754|2026-09.headline: Kissht Q2 FY27: AUM up 68% YoY to Rs 9,317 crore and PAT doubled to Rs 125 crore, with credit cost down to 6.2% of AUM.
544754|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed growth alongside lower risk: AUM rose 16.4% QoQ to Rs 9,317 crore, PAT rose 31.6% QoQ to Rs 125 crore, and ROAA reached 5.78%. Asset quality improved on most measures, with Gross NPA at 2.18%, Stage-2 at 2.37%, and credit cost at 6.2% of average AUM. Cost of borrowing fell to 13.76% from 14.45%. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 60%+ and impairment reduction guidance to more than 15% YoY, and completed a Rs 832 crore preferential allotment.

qa_highlights.question: AUM is up 68% while customers grew about 21-22%. What is driving AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three drivers: deeper repeat-customer lending with higher repeat ticket sizes, a shift to higher-quality customers with larger tickets, and slightly longer tenures.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company balance lower funding costs passed to customers against ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost of funds, operating leverage and lower risk cost let it pass part of the benefit to customers while keeping ROA and ROE at past levels plus a cushion. NCD raises were about 150 bps below the 13.76% blended cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of funds fall 12% QoQ, and is there room for more?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan said the 12.1% incremental borrowing rate will flow through over 3-4 quarters as legacy debt rolls off, implying at least 150 bps reduction, possibly more.

qa_highlights.question: How are better-quality customers being acquired, and at what CAC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited app campaigns targeting income above Rs 1 lakh per month, aggregator partnerships (UPI, broking, wealth) in the top 30 centres, and a stronger Apple app mix. qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to 19% from 26%?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for operating leverage, given opex grew faster than income?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan said about 50% of opex is indirect fixed cost and opex to AUM should improve 40-50 bps QoQ for many quarters, with the later clarification of 25-40 bps. Management would invest in collections or AI if stress emerged.

Management said capacity will rise from about 6.15 lakh tons to nearly 7 lakh tons by FY27, with the Shoolagiri and Bawal plants coming online this year. 544777|2026-06.headline: CMR Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore and PAT 22% to INR68 crore, with EBITDA/kg at about INR12.40 but operating cash flow negative.
544777|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore, EBITDA rose 27% to INR139 crore and PAT rose 22% to over INR68 crore, with aluminium volumes up 25% YoY. Management stressed EBITDA per kg (about INR12.40) over percentage margin because aluminium is largely a pass-through. Operating cash flow was negative due to a roughly 40% rise in average realisation (from about INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg), which raised working capital; inventory days fell to 40 from 45 and the cash conversion cycle to 65 days from 69. Management kept INR12/kg EBITDA and 25% FY27 volume growth as internal targets, while the Odisha plant ramps up.

segments.commentary: Billets volume +149% YoY and UBC volume +333% YoY, both in ramp-up mode. Management cites construction, renewables, electrical and industrial demand beyond automotive.

Odisha (Hindalco, 48,000 tpa) must reach about 4,000 tons a month from about 6,000 tons for the quarter to hit full utilisation within FY27; Hindustan Zinc MoU has no definitive agreement or construction start.

Hedging of secondary aluminium relies on a balance between cost-plus auto pricing and LME hedges; the INR36 crore cash flow hedge entry in other expenses and the reclassification of FX and commodity hedge ineffectiveness from other income into adjusted EBITDA affect comparability with prior presentations.
